The Pro Patria Journalism Awards: The Rotary Club of Manila's Enduring Tribute to Truth, Press Freedom, and Nation-Building PE Reginald T. Yu A Vision Beyond Recognition INSTITUTIONS are often remembered for the buildings they erect, the programs they launch, or the leaders they produce. Yet some of the most enduring legacies are those that champion ideas—ideas that continue to shape society long after the names of their founders have faded into history. Among the many distinguished projects undertaken by the Rotary Club of Manila throughout its storied existence, few have exercised as profound an influence on public life as the Journalism Awards. Conceived during a period when the Philippines was navigating the complexities of a young democracy, the Awards emerged from a simple but powerful conviction: that a free, responsible, and courageous press is indispensable to nation building. The Rotary Club of Manila has always understood that service extends beyond charitable works and community projects. Service also means strengthening the institutions upon which a democratic society depends. Among these institutions, none is more vital than a press capable of informing citizens, scrutinizing power, and fostering meaningful public discourse. It was from this understanding that the Journalism Awards were born. In 1966, as the nation observed National Press Week, the Rotary Club of Manila adopted what would become one of its most enduring and prestigious projects. Under the leadership of President Jose M. Olbes and the Club's Board of Directors, the Journalism Awards were designated as the Major Club Project of the Year. What began as a gesture of support for Philippine journalism would evolve into a tradition that has endured for nearly six decades. Few could have anticipated the significance the project would eventually attain. What started as an annual recognition program would become a living chronicle of Philippine journalism itself —a record of the individuals, institutions, and ideals that have shaped the nation's understanding of truth, accountability, and public service. The Birth of a Tradition The first Journalism Awards ceremony took place in February 1968 during the presidency of Gil R. Carlos. The inaugural honorees immediately established the standards that would define the Awards for generations. Armando E. Doronila, whose distinguished career would later make him one of the country's most respected journalists and public intellectuals, was recognized as Journalist of the Year. Manila Times was named Newspaper of the Year, setting a precedent for honoring not only individual excellence but also institutional leadership within the profession. The significance of that first ceremony extended far beyond the presentation of trophies. It signaled the Rotary Club of Manila's recognition that journalism was not merely a profession but a public trust. The Awards sought to celebrate individuals who demonstrated excellence in reporting, analysis, commentary, and editorial leadership while remaining committed to the broader interests of society. As the program gained momentum, the list of honorees began to reflect the remarkable breadth of Philippine journalism. Journalists from national newspapers, provincial publications, radio stations, and emerging broadcast outlets found themselves recognized for their contributions to public understanding. The Journalism Awards quickly acquired a reputation for seriousness and credibility. To be recognized by the Rotary Club of Manila was to receive acknowledgment not merely from fellow journalists but from one of the country's most respected civic institutions. The Quill and the Flame Every great institution possesses symbols that embody its ideals. For the Journalism Awards, that symbol emerged through the creative vision of Rotarian Tomas C. Banguis Jr., President of AB Communications. The trophy he designed was both elegant and meaningful. Its most prominent feature was a stylized quill pen, crafted from wood and brass, mounted upon a carefully designed base. Behind it stood an etched glass bearing the Rotary Club of Manila emblem. The symbolism was unmistakable. The quill represented the written word—the journalist's timeless instrument. Long before computers, smartphones, and digital platforms transformed newsrooms, the pen served as the primary tool through which facts were recorded, stories were told, and truths were preserved. The brass flame suggested something equally important: enlightenment. It evoked the idea that journalism illuminates darkness, exposes hidden realities, and brings clarity to public discourse. Together, the quill and the flame formed a powerful visual metaphor for journalism's highest purpose. Over the decades, the trophy underwent refinements and modifications, but its essential meaning remained unchanged. It continued to symbolize courage, integrity, and the pursuit of truth. Honoring the Guardians of Public Trust From its earliest years, the Journalism Awards distinguished themselves by embracing the diversity of the journalistic profession. The Awards did not confine themselves to a single medium or category. They recognized reporters and columnists, investigative journalists and editors, broadcasters and publishers. They honored newspapers, radio stations, television networks, magazines, and later, digital platforms. This broad perspective reflected an understanding that journalism functions as an ecosystem. Democracy depends not only upon prominent national newspapers but also upon community publications serving local audiences. It relies not only upon television anchors and radio commentators but also upon investigative reporters who spend months uncovering facts that others would prefer remain hidden. The Journalism Awards recognized excellence wherever it could be found. As the years progressed, categories expanded to include business journalism, community journalism, feature writing, photojournalism, public affairs programming, documentary production, investigative reporting, opinion writing, and eventually new media. Each addition reflected the evolving realities of the profession while reinforcing the Awards' central mission: to celebrate journalism that serves the public interest. When the Quill Fell Silent The history of the Journalism Awards cannot be separated from the broader history of Philippine democracy. In the early 1970s, the nation entered one of the most consequential periods in its modern history. The declaration of Martial Law dramatically altered the landscape of public discourse and press freedom. As media institutions faced restrictions and independent journalism became increasingly difficult, the Journalism Awards entered a prolonged period of dormancy. For more than a decade, the annual ceremonies ceased. The suspension carried profound symbolic significance. The Journalism Awards had been established to honor freedom of expression, independent reporting, and the public's right to know. In an environment where those principles faced significant challenges, the absence of the Awards became a poignant reflection of the circumstances confronting the Philippine press. The silence of the Awards spoke volumes. It served as a reminder that journalism flourishes only where freedom exists, and that the recognition of journalistic excellence is meaningful only when journalists are free to pursue truth without fear. The Return of Press Freedom The restoration of democracy following the people power Revolution Of 1986 marked a turning point not only for the nation but also for the Journalism Awards. The Rotary Club of Manila revived the program during a pericxl of renewed optimism and democratic rebuilding. The return of the Awards symbolized more than the resumption of an annual tradition. It represented the reaffirmation of principles that had guided the project since its inception. The revival coincided with a remarkable renaissance in Philippine journalism. News organizations regained their independence. Investigative reporting flourished. Editorial voices multiplied. Public affairs programming expanded. Journalists once again exercised their role as watchdogs of democracy. The Journalism Awards returned at precisely the moment when the nation needed them most.
They became both a celebration of journalistic excellence and a tribute to the resilience Of those who had defended the profession through difficult times. Chronicling a Changing Media Landscape Few professions have undergone as dramatic a transformation as journalism. The world that produced the first Journalism Awards in 1968 was dominated by newspapers and radio. Television was still developing as a major source of information. News traveled at a pace that seems almost unimaginable today. Over the decades, technology reshaped the profession repeatedly. Television emerged as a dominant force in national discourse. Twenty-four-hour news cycles accelerated reporting. Cable networks expanded coverage. The internet revolutionized information delivery. Social media transformed audience engagement. Smartphones placed newsrooms in the pockets of ordinary citizens. Through every transformation, the Journalism Awards evolved. New categories recognized emerging forms of storytelling and communication. Investigative documentaries, online journalism, digital reporting, and multimedia productions found places alongside traditional forms of journalism. The Awards demonstrated an unusual ability to adapt without sacrificing their fundamental values. Technology changed. Standards did not. A Hall Of Honor As the Awards matured, it became increasingly evident that certain journalists had achieved a level of excellence that transcended annual recognition. To acknowledge these extraordinary contributions, the Journalism Awards established a Hall of Fame. The roster of inductees reads like a pantheon of modern Philippine journalism. Maximo Soliven, whose columns shaped public opinion for generations. Teodoro Benigno Jr., whose incisive commentary illuminated national issues. Armando Doronila, whose reporting and analysis influenced both journalism and public policy. Jessica Soho, whose investigative work redefined broadcast journalism. Conrado de Quiros, whose essays blended intellect, wit, and social critique. Ricardo Puno Jr., Jose Taruc, Jarius Bondoc, Howie Severino, Rey Langit, and many others whose work left indelible marks on the profession. These Hall of Fame honorees represent more than personal achievement. They embody journalism's highest ideals. The Provinces Speak One of the most admirable aspects of the Journalism Awards has been its recognition that journalism's most important work is often performed far from the nation's capital. Provincial newspapers, community broadcasters, and regional journalists have long played critical roles in informing citizens, exposing local issues, and fostering civic engagement. The Awards consistently recognized these contributions. Publications from Cebu, Davao, Baguio, Bacolod, Cagayan de Oro, Zamboanga, and numerous other regions received recognition alongside national media institutions. This commitment reflected an understanding that democracy is strongest when citizens are informed not only about national affairs but also about the realities affecting their own communities. The Journalism Awards became one of the few national programs to consistently celebrate excellence in regional journalism. Journalism in Service of Democracy The true significance of the Journalism Awards lies not in trophies, ceremonies, or citations. It lies in the values they affrm. At their core, the Awards recognize journalism as an essential pillar of democratic society. Every honored reporter, broadcaster, editor, publisher, photographer, or commentator contributes to a larger mission: enabling citizens to make informed decisions. Investigative reporting promotes accountability.
Editorial commentary stimulates public debate.
Community journalism strengthens governance.
Documentary storytelling preserves collective memory.
Broadcast journalism brings information to millions. Together, these functions fortn the foundation of an informed citizenry. The Journalism Awards celebrate not merely professional competence but civic contribution. Pro Patria: For Country In 2021, under the Chairmanship of Dean Amado "Amading" Valdez, the Journalism Awards acquired a name that perfectly captured their deeper purpose. The title Pro Patria Journalism Awards was suggested by veteran journalist, publisher, commentator, and fellow Rotarian Antonio Tony" Lopez, one of country's most accomplished media practitioners. The phrase means "For Country." Its adoption transformed the Awards into something larger than a recognition program. It articulated a philosophy. The title acknowledges that journalism, at its highest level, is an act of service. The pursuit of truth is not undertaken solely for professional advancement or institutional prestige. It is undertaken for the benefit of society itself. Every journalist honored under the Pro Patria banner has contributed to the nation's understanding of itself. They have informed public debate, challenged complacency, exposed wrongdoing. and strengthened democratic institutions. In doing so, they have served their country. The Awards in the Digital Age The twenty-first century has introduced unprecedented challenges to journalism. The rise of social media, misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence, and declining public trust has complicated the profession in ways earlier generations could scarcely have imagined. Yet these challenges have also underscored the continuing relevance of the Journalism Awards. At a time when facts are increasingly contested and information moves instantaneously across digital networks, the need for ethical, accurate, and responsible journalism has become more important than ever. The Awards continue to evolve alongside the profession while remaining rooted in timeless principles of truth, fairness, accountability, and public service. The Rotary Club of Manila and the Defense of Truth The Journalism Awards stand as one of the clearest expressions of the Rotary Club of Manila's belief that civic leadership extends beyond philanthropy. For decades, the Club has demonstrated that strengthening democratic institutions is itself a form of service. By recognizing journalists, the Rotary Club of Manila affirms the importance of transparency, accountability, informed citizenship, and public discourse. It acknowledges that a society cannot address its challenges effectively unless its citizens have access to accurate and trustworthy information. The Journalism Awards therefore represent more than support for media. They represent support for democracy itself. The Legacy Continues Today, nearly sixty years after the first Journalism Awards were presented, the iconic quill continues to symbolize a noble and necessary profession. Generations of journalists have received its recognition. Newspapers have risen and fallen. Technologies have changed. Political eras have come and gone. Yet the principles underlying the Awards remain remarkably constant. Truth remains essential.
Freedom remains precious.
Journalism remains indispensable. The Rotary Club of Manila's Pro Patria Journalism Awards endure because they speak to these timeless realities. They remind us that societies progress when facts prevail over falsehoods, when accountability triumphs over secrecy, and when citizens are empowered by knowledge rather than deprived of it. As long as journalists continue to pursue truth and serve the public, the quill will remain raised. And as long as the Rotary Club of Manila continues to champion those ideals, the Pro Patria Journalism Awards will remain one of the country's most meaningful tributes to journalism in the service of nation, democracy, and freedom. Pro Patria.
For Country.
For Truth.
For Generations Yet to Come. Journalism in the Service of Country – The 2026 Journalism Pro Patria Honorees PE Reginald T. Yu THIS year's Journalism Pro Patria Honorees represent the very best of Philippine journalism. Through decades of dedication, courage, integrity, and excellence, they have not only chronicled history but helped shape it. Their careers stand as enduring reminders that journalism, at its finest, is more than a profession — it is a public trust and a service to country. The Rotary Club of Manila proudly pays tribute to these distinguished media leaders whose legacy continues to inspire the profession and the nation they have faithfully served. ELIMOTOUR
Vlogger of the Year In an era where information travels at the speed of a click and audiences increasingly turn to digital platforms for news, insights, and inspiration, ELIMOTOUR has distinguished itself as a pioneering force in Filipino digital storytelling. More than a travel vlogger, ELIMOTOUR has become a cultural ambassador, educator, and chronicler of experiences, bringing audiences closer to the people, places, and stories that define the richness of the Philippines and the wider world. Through compelling visuals, thoughtful narration, and a remarkable ability to connect with viewers, ELIMOTOUR has transformed travel content into a meaningful journalistic endeavor. His work goes beyond showcasing destinations. It documents local traditions, celebrates cultural heritage, highlights community initiatives, and fosters a deeper appreciation for the diversity that shapes the Filipino identity. Every episode reflects meticulous preparation, authenticity, and an unwavering commitment to presenting truthful and engaging content. In a digital landscape often dominated by fleeting trends and superficial entertainment, ELIMOTOUR has consistently demonstrated that online platforms can be powerful tools for education, cultural understanding, and public engagement. His influence has encouraged responsible tourism, inspired countless viewers to explore and appreciate their own country, and provided exposure to local communities that might otherwise remain unseen. For elevating digital content creation into a platform for learning and discovery; for exemplifying integrity, creativity, and excellence in online storytelling; and for inspiring audiences through meaningful and impactful narratives, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly confers upon ELIMOTOUR the Journalism Award for Vlogger of the Year. BOMBO RADYO
Radio Station of the Year For generations of Filipinos, Bombo Radyo has been more than a radio station — it has been a trusted companion, a reliable source of information, and a steadfast guardian of public interest. Through decades of dedicated service, Bombo Radyo has built an enduring legacy founded upon journalistic integrity, community engagement, and an unwavering commitment to truth. Its extensive network has enabled it to reach urban centers and remote communities alike, ensuring that timely news, public affairs discussions, and critical information remain accessible to millions of listeners throughout the country. Whether reporting on national developments, local concerns, natural disasters, or matters of public safety, Bombo Radyo has consistently demonstrated the essential role of radio as a lifeline of information and a pillar of democracy. What distinguishes Bombo Radyo is its deep connection to the communities it serves. Its broadcasters and reporters understand the pulse of the nation because they remain close to the people whose stories they tell. This commitment to grassroots journalism has fostered trust among audiences and reinforced the station's reputation as one of the country's most credible and influential broadcast institutions. In a rapidly evolving media environment, Bombo Radyo has successfully adapted to new technologies while preserving the core values that have guided its mission for decades. Its dedication to public set-vice, factual reporting, and civic responsibility continues to set a standard for excellence in Philippine broadcasting. For its outstanding contribution to radio journalism, its steadfast commitment to informing and empowering the Filipino people, and its enduring legacy of public service, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly honors Bombo Radyo as Radio Station of the Year. ANGELO B. PALMONES
Radio Personality of the Year Throughout a distinguished career in broadcasting and public communication, Angelo Palmones has demonstrated how journalism can serve as a bridge between knowledge and society. As a respected broadcaster, educator, and advocate for science and evidence-based discourse, he has consistently elevated the quality of public conversation through insightful reporting and responsible communication. Known for his intellectual rigor and clarity of expression, Palmones possesses the rare ability to translate complex scientific, technological, and public policy issues into language that resonates with ordinary Citizens. His work has empowered audiences to better understand the challenges and opportunities facing society, enabling them to make more informed decisions as citizens and stakeholders in nation-building. Beyond his accomplishments as a broadcaster, he has championed the values of critical thinking, factual accuracy, and public accountability. In an age where misinformation and sensationalism often threaten informed discourse, Angelo Palmones has remained steadfast in his commitment to truth and responsible journalism. His professionalism, credibility, and dedication to public education have earned him the respect of colleagues and listeners alike. His contributions exemplify the enduring power of radio as a platform for enlightenment and civic engagement. Through every broadcast, he has demonstrated that journalism is not merely about reporting events but about helping citizens understand their significance and implications. For his exceptional contributions to radio broadcasting, his dedication to public education, and his steadfast commitment to responsible journalism, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly presents Angelo Palmones with the Journalism Award for Radio Personality of the Year. GMA Network
Television Station of the Year For more than seven decades, GMA Network has stood as one of the Philippines' most respected and influential media institutions. Through its commitment to journalistic excellence, technological innovation, and public sew-ice, it has become a trusted source of information for millions of Filipinos both at home and abroad. At the heart of GMA Network's success lies its unwavering dedication to delivering accurate, balanced, and timely news. Its journalists, producers, and media professionals have consistently demonstrated courage and professionalism in covering events of national significance, often under challenging circumstances. From elections and natural disasters to social issues and international developments, GMA Network has provided audiences with comprehensive coverage grounded in the principles of fairness and truth. Beyond news reporting, GMA Network has continuously expanded the boundaries of broadcast journalism through innovative programming, investigative reporting, and public affairs initiatives that encourage informed public discourse. Its commitment to leveraging technology has allowed it to reach audiences across multiple platforms, ensuring that credible information remains accessible in an increasingly digital world. Throughout its history, GMA Network has upheld the essential role of a free and responsible press in strengthening democratic institutions and empowering citizens. Its contributions have helped shape national conversations, promote accountability, and foster a better-informed society. For its enduring commitment to journalistic excellence, public service, and innovation in broadcasting, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly recognizes GMA Network as Television Station of the Year. ALFONSO TOMAS P. ARAULLO
TV Journalist of the Year Among the most respected journalists of his generation, Atom Araullo has distinguished himself through courage, compassion, and an unwavering commitment to telling stories that matter. Throughout his career, he has consistently brought viewers beyond the headlines and into the lives of individuals and communities whose experiences illuminate the most pressing issues of our time. Renowned for his immersive reporting and investigative journalism, Araullo has covered natural disasters, humanitarian crises, environmental challenges, social inequalities, and stories of resilience across the Philippines and around the world. His work reflects a profound understanding that journalism is ultimately about people — their struggles, aspirations, and dignity. What sets Atom Araullo apart is his ability to combine meticulous reporting with genuine empathy. He approaches every assignment with intellectual rigor and human sensitivity, ensuring that complex issues are presented with both accuracy and context. Through his reporting, audiences gain not only information but a Iso a deeper appreciation of the realities faced by fellow citizens. In an era marked by rapid information flows and increasing public skepticism, Atom Araullo has remained a steadfast advocate for truth, accountability, and responsible journalism. His work embodies the highest ideals of the profession and serves as an inspiration to aspiring journalists across the nation. For his exceptional achievements in television journalism, his fearless pursuit of truth, and his enduring commitment to public service through story telling. the Rotary Club of Manila proudly confers upon Atom Araullo the Journalism Award for TV Journalist of the Year. BUSINESSMIRROR
Newspaper of the Year Since its founding, BusinessMirror has earned a distinguished reputation as one of the country's most credible and insightful newspapers. While widely recognized for its comprehensive coverage of business and economic affairs. it has also established itself as a trusted Source Of reporting on governance, public policy, environment, agriculture, education, and social development. At a time when economic decisions increasingly influence the lives of ordinary citizens, BusinessMirror has played a vital role in helping readers understand the forces shaping the nation's future. Through balanced reporting, thoughtful analysis, and rigorous editorial standards, it has provided clarity on complex issues that affect businesses, government institutions, and communities alike. Its journalists and editors have consistently demonstrated a commitment to independence, and public accountability. By presenting facts within their broader social and economic contexts, BusinessMirror has enriched public discourse and empowered readers to engage more meaningfully with issues of national importance. Beyond reporting events, BusinessMirror contributes to nation-building by fostering informed decision-making among policymakers, business leaders, and citizens. Its dedication to excellence reflects the essential role of quality journalism in promoting transparency, economic progress, and democratic participation. For its outstanding contributions to Philippine journalism, its commitment to informing and enlightening the public, and its consistent pursuit of editorial excellence, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly honors BusinessMirror as Newspaper of the Year. JARIUS Y. BONDOC
Opinion Writer of the Year For decades, Jarius Bondoc has stood among the most respected voices in Philippine opinion journalism. Through incisive commentary, fearless analysis, and an unwavering commitment to accountability, he has consistently challenged institutions, exposed wrongdoing, and advocated for the public interest. His columns are distinguished not merely by eloquence but by substance. Combining investigative rigor with thoughtful interpretation, Bondoc has demonstrated how opinion writing can serve as a powerful instrument for transparency, reform, and civic engagement. His work reflects a deep understanding of governance, public policy, and the issues that affect the lives of ordinary Filipinos. Throughout his distinguished career, he has shown remarkable courage in addressing controversial topics and holding those in positions of power accountable. At a time when independent voices remain essential to the health of democratic societies, Jarius Bondoc has exemplified the vital role of opinion journalism in fostering informed debate and encouraging responsible governance. His writings continue to influence public discourse and inspire both readers and fellow journalists to value truth, integrity, and intellectual honesty. Through his persistent pursuit of facts and justice, he has reinforced the public's faith in journalism as a force for positive change. For his distinguished career, his outstanding contribution to public discourse, and his steadfast dedication to truth and accountability, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly presents Jarius Bondoc with the Journalism Award for Opinion Writer of the Year. CHRISTIAN V. ESGUERRA
Online Individual Journalist of the Year As journalism continues to evolve in the digital age, Christian Esguerra has emerged as one of the Philippines' most respected and influential online journalists. Through his widely followed platform, Facts First, he has demonstrated that digital media can serve not only as a source of information but also as a venue for meaningful dialogue, critical analysis, and civic engagement. Esguerra has earned the trust of audiences through his unwavering commitment to factual reporting, thoughtful interviews, and evidence-based commentary. In an environment increasingly challenged by misinformation, polarization, and declining public trust, he has consistently upheld the fundamental principles of journalism— accuracy, fairness, independence, and accountability. His interviews bring together policymakers, experts, thought leaders, and stakeholders to discuss issues of national significance with depth and clarity. By encouraging informed discussion rather than sensationalism, he has elevated the quality of public discourse and empowered citizens to engage more thoughtfully with the issues shaping their communities and the nation. Christian Esguerra's work exemplifies how journalists can adapt to new platforms without compromising professional standards. His dedication to truth and public service demonstrates that credible journalism remains indispensable regardless of the medium through which it is delivered. PRES. RAOUL C. CREENCIA 34th Weekly Membership Meeting Editorial  Reginald T. Yu Editor-in-Chief IN every generation, societies are ultimately shaped by the quality of the information upon which their citizens act. Governments make decisions.
Businesses allocate capital.
Communities respond to crises.
Families form opinions.
Democracies elect leaders.
Yet all these depend upon one indispensable foundation: truth. That is why journalism matters. For nearly six decades, the Rotary Club of Manila Journalism Awards have stood as one of the nation's most enduring tributes to those who dedicate their lives to seeking, verifying, and communicating the truth. Long before social media transformed the information landscape, long before algorithms amplified voices both credible and questionable, the Rotary Club of Manila recognized that a free and responsible press is essential to a free and responsible society. Today, that conviction is more relevant than ever. We live in an age of unprecedented connectivity. Information travels across continents in seconds. News breaks instantly. Opinions spread virally. Artificial intelligence generates content at remarkable speed. Yet amid this abundance of information lies a growing challenge: distinguishing fact from fiction, evidence from speculation, and journalism from mere noise. The role of the journalist has therefore become not less important, but more important than ever. A journalist's task is not simply to report events. It is to provide context amid confusion, clarity amid complexity, and accountability amid power. It requires courage to ask difficult questions, discipline to verify facts, integrity to resist pressure, and humility to place truth above personal preference. The finest journalists serve not political interests, commercial interests, or ideological interests. They serve the public interest. That commitment has often come at considerable personal cost. Throughout history, journalists have faced intimidation, censorship, threats, and even violence. Yet many have persevered because they understood that silence in the face of falsehood is not neutrality—it is surrender. The Rotary Club of Manila Journalism Awards were established to honor precisely this spirit. Over the decades, the awards have recognized some of the most respected names in Philippine media—men and women whose work informed the nation, challenged complacency, exposed wrongdoing, elevated public discourse, and inspired future generations of journalists. Their achievements remind us that journalism, at its best, is a public service. The Journalism Awards are therefore more than a recognition program. They are a statement of values. They affirm that truth matters. They affirm that facts matter. They affirm that responsible journalism remains indispensable to national development, good governance, and democratic progress. As Rotary's theme this year calls upon us to Unite for Good, we recognize that meaningful unity cannot be built upon misinformation, division, or ignorance. Genuine progress requires informed citizens capable of making thoughtful decisions. It requires institutions committed to transparency. It requires journalists who continue to illuminate issues that affect the lives of millions. The Rotary Club of Manila salutes all those who have devoted their talents, intellect, and courage to this noble profession. May they continue to remind us that while technology changes, platforms evolve, and headlines fade, the pursuit of truth remains timeless. For in the end, societies flourish not merely because they are prosperous, but because they are informed. And informed societies are built by journalists who have the courage to tell the truth. Pro Patria and Outstanding Journalism: A Natural Alliance of Truth and Nationhood  President's Message TODAY, the Rotary Club Of Manila proudly celebrates one Of its most cherished and enduring signature projects — the Pro Patria Journalism Awards. It is especially fitting that we gather today on the eve of our nation's celebration of independence. As the Philippines marks another year of freedom and nationhood, we are reminded that a truly independent nation is sustained not only by brave heroes of the past, but also by courageous voices of the present – journalists who speak truth to power, give voice to the people, and safeguard the public's right to know. In every democratic society, journalism occupies a sacred space between power and the people. It informs citizens, shapes public discourse, exposes wrongdoing, and preserves truth against distortion. Yet journalism is not merely about reporting events or chasing headlines. At its highest form, journalism is an act of patriotism. Indeed, pro-patria and responsible journalism are synonymous. They go hand in hand because both are ultimately anchored on a common purpose: the welfare and advancement of the nation. To be pro-patria means to act for the good of one's country. It is a commitment to uphold national interests, protect democratic institutions, and strengthen the moral and civic foundations of society. Responsible journalism pursues exactly the same objectives. It seeks truth not to destroy, but to enlighten; not to divide, but to guide society toward justice, accountability, and progress. A responsible journalist understands that the power of the press carries enormous influence. Words can inspire unity or provoke discord. News can educate citizens or manipulate public opinion. In an era dominated by misinformation, sensationalism, and digital noise, the duty of journalists has become even more critical. Patriotism in journalism does not mean blind loyalty to government or the suppression of criticism. On the contrary, genuine love of country requires courage to speak truth to power when necessary. It demands vigilance against corruption, abuse, and incompetence because these weaken the nation from within. History has repeatedly shown that nations flourish when journalism remains principled and responsible. Investigative reporting has uncovered corruption, defended human rights, and amplified the voices of the marginalized. Journalists who expose wrongdoing often do so not out of hostility toward their country, but out of profound belief that the nation deserves better leadership, better governance, and better institutions. In this sense, responsible journalism becomes an indispensable pillar of nation-building. At the same time, patriotism imposes discipline upon the practice of journalism. Responsible journalists verify facts before publication, avoid reckless accusations, and reject sensationalism designed solely for profit or popularity. They understand that false information can erode public trust, inflame social tensions, and damage democratic stability. A journalist who deliberately spreads misinformation in pursuit of ratings or influence cannot claim to serve the country. National interest is never advanced by deception. Responsible journalism also nurtures informed citizenship. Democracies thrive when citizens are equipped with accurate information and thoughtful analysis. Through ethical reporting, journalists empower people to participate meaningfully in public life. make sound decisions, and hold leaders accountable. In this way, journalism strengthens democracy itself — one of the highest expressions of patriotism. Ultimately, pro-patria and responsible journalism are inseparable because both seek truth, justice, accountability, and the common good. They are not opposing ideals, but complementary duties. A journalist who genuinely loves country serves the people with honesty, fairness, courage, and integrity. And a nation that values patriotism must equally value a free, ethical, and responsible press. articles.title: Roll of Honor: Notable Laureates of the Rotary Club of Manila Pro Patria Journalism Awards

body.text: FOR nearly sixty years, the Rotary Club of Manila Journalism Awards—now known as the Pro Patria Journalism Awards — have recognized many of the most respected names in Philippine media. The roster of awardees reads like a who's who of modern Philippine journalism, encompassing newspaper editors, investigative reporters, broadcasters, publishers, documentary producers, commentators, media institutions, and champions of press freedom.
The following roll of honor highlights some of the most distinguished individuals and organizations recognized through the decades.

The Founding Years
1968–1973
The first generation of awardees established the standards of excellence that would define the Awards for decades.

articles.title: The Pro Patria Journalism Awards: The Rotary Club of Manila's Enduring Tribute to Truth, Press Freedom, and Nation-Building

body.text: A Vision Beyond Recognition

INSTITUTIONS are often remembered for the buildings they erect, the programs they launch, or the leaders they produce. Yet some of the most enduring legacies are those that champion ideas—ideas that continue to shape society long after the names of their founders have faded into history.

Among the many distinguished projects undertaken by the Rotary Club of Manila throughout its storied existence, few have exercised as profound an influence on public life as the Journalism Awards. Conceived during a period when the Philippines was navigating the complexities of a young democracy, the Awards emerged from a simple but powerful conviction: that a free, responsible, and courageous press is indispensable to nation building.

The Rotary Club of Manila has always understood that service extends beyond charitable works and community projects. Service also means strengthening the institutions upon which a democratic society depends. Among these institutions, none is more vital than a press capable of informing citizens, scrutinizing power, and fostering meaningful public discourse.
It was from this understanding that the Journalism Awards were born.

In 1966, as the nation observed National Press Week, the Rotary Club of Manila adopted what would become one of its most enduring and prestigious projects. Under the leadership of President Jose M. Olbes and the Club's Board of Directors, the Journalism Awards were designated as the Major Club Project of the Year. What began as a gesture of support for Philippine journalism would evolve into a tradition that has endured for nearly six decades.
Few could have anticipated the significance the project would eventually attain.

What started as an annual recognition program would become a living chronicle of Philippine journalism itself —a record of the individuals, institutions, and ideals that have shaped the nation's understanding of truth, accountability, and public service.
The Birth of a Tradition
The first Journalism Awards ceremony took place in February 1968 during the presidency of Gil R. Carlos.

The inaugural honorees immediately established the standards that would define the Awards for generations. Armando E. Doronila, whose distinguished career would later make him one of the country's most respected journalists and public intellectuals, was recognized as Journalist of the Year. Manila Times was named Newspaper of the Year, setting a precedent for honoring not only individual excellence but also institutional leadership within the profession.
The significance of that first ceremony extended far beyond the presentation of trophies.
It signaled the Rotary Club of Manila's recognition that journalism was not merely a profession but a public trust.
The Awards sought to celebrate individuals who demonstrated excellence in reporting, analysis, commentary, and editorial leadership while remaining committed to the broader interests of society.

As the program gained momentum, the list of honorees began to reflect the remarkable breadth of Philippine journalism. Journalists from national newspapers, provincial publications, radio stations, and emerging broadcast outlets found themselves recognized for their contributions to public understanding.

The Journalism Awards quickly acquired a reputation for seriousness and credibility. To be recognized by the Rotary Club of Manila was to receive acknowledgment not merely from fellow journalists but from one of the country's most respected civic institutions.
The Quill and the Flame
Every great institution possesses symbols that embody its ideals.
For the Journalism Awards, that symbol emerged through the creative vision of Rotarian Tomas C. Banguis Jr., President of AB Communications.

The trophy he designed was both elegant and meaningful. Its most prominent feature was a stylized quill pen, crafted from wood and brass, mounted upon a carefully designed base. Behind it stood an etched glass bearing the Rotary Club of Manila emblem.
The symbolism was unmistakable.

The quill represented the written word—the journalist's timeless instrument. Long before computers, smartphones, and digital platforms transformed newsrooms, the pen served as the primary tool through which facts were recorded, stories were told, and truths were preserved.
The brass flame suggested something equally important: enlightenment.

It evoked the idea that journalism illuminates darkness, exposes hidden realities, and brings clarity to public discourse. Together, the quill and the flame formed a powerful visual metaphor for journalism's highest purpose.
Over the decades, the trophy underwent refinements and modifications, but its essential meaning remained unchanged. It continued to symbolize courage, integrity, and the pursuit of truth.
Honoring the Guardians of Public Trust
From its earliest years, the Journalism Awards distinguished themselves by embracing the diversity of the journalistic profession.

The Awards did not confine themselves to a single medium or category. They recognized reporters and columnists, investigative journalists and editors, broadcasters and publishers. They honored newspapers, radio stations, television networks, magazines, and later, digital platforms.
This broad perspective reflected an understanding that journalism functions as an ecosystem.

Democracy depends not only upon prominent national newspapers but also upon community publications serving local audiences. It relies not only upon television anchors and radio commentators but also upon investigative reporters who spend months uncovering facts that others would prefer remain hidden.
The Journalism Awards recognized excellence wherever it could be found.

As the years progressed, categories expanded to include business journalism, community journalism, feature writing, photojournalism, public affairs programming, documentary production, investigative reporting, opinion writing, and eventually new media.
Each addition reflected the evolving realities of the profession while reinforcing the Awards' central mission: to celebrate journalism that serves the public interest.
When the Quill Fell Silent
The history of the Journalism Awards cannot be separated from the broader history of Philippine democracy.

In the early 1970s, the nation entered one of the most consequential periods in its modern history. The declaration of Martial Law dramatically altered the landscape of public discourse and press freedom.
As media institutions faced restrictions and independent journalism became increasingly difficult, the Journalism Awards entered a prolonged period of dormancy.
For more than a decade, the annual ceremonies ceased.
The suspension carried profound symbolic significance.

The Journalism Awards had been established to honor freedom of expression, independent reporting, and the public's right to know. In an environment where those principles faced significant challenges, the absence of the Awards became a poignant reflection of the circumstances confronting the Philippine press.
The silence of the Awards spoke volumes.

It served as a reminder that journalism flourishes only where freedom exists, and that the recognition of journalistic excellence is meaningful only when journalists are free to pursue truth without fear.
The Return of Press Freedom
The restoration of democracy following the people power Revolution Of 1986 marked a turning point not only for the nation but also for the Journalism Awards.

The Rotary Club of Manila revived the program during a pericxl of renewed optimism and democratic rebuilding. The return of the Awards symbolized more than the resumption of an annual tradition. It represented the reaffirmation of principles that had guided the project since its inception.
The revival coincided with a remarkable renaissance in Philippine journalism.

News organizations regained their independence. Investigative reporting flourished. Editorial voices multiplied. Public affairs programming expanded. Journalists once again exercised their role as watchdogs of democracy.

The Journalism Awards returned at precisely the moment when the nation needed them most.
They became both a celebration of journalistic excellence and a tribute to the resilience Of those who had defended the profession through difficult times.
Chronicling a Changing Media Landscape
Few professions have undergone as dramatic a transformation as journalism.

The world that produced the first Journalism Awards in 1968 was dominated by newspapers and radio. Television was still developing as a major source of information. News traveled at a pace that seems almost unimaginable today.
Over the decades, technology reshaped the profession repeatedly.

Television emerged as a dominant force in national discourse. Twenty-four-hour news cycles accelerated reporting. Cable networks expanded coverage. The internet revolutionized information delivery. Social media transformed audience engagement. Smartphones placed newsrooms in the pockets of ordinary citizens.
Through every transformation, the Journalism Awards evolved.

New categories recognized emerging forms of storytelling and communication. Investigative documentaries, online journalism, digital reporting, and multimedia productions found places alongside traditional forms of journalism.
The Awards demonstrated an unusual ability to adapt without sacrificing their fundamental values.
Technology changed. Standards did not.
A Hall Of Honor
As the Awards matured, it became increasingly evident that certain journalists had achieved a level of excellence that transcended annual recognition.
To acknowledge these extraordinary contributions, the Journalism Awards established a Hall of Fame.
The roster of inductees reads like a pantheon of modern Philippine journalism.

Maximo Soliven, whose columns shaped public opinion for generations. Teodoro Benigno Jr., whose incisive commentary illuminated national issues. Armando Doronila, whose reporting and analysis influenced both journalism and public policy. Jessica Soho, whose investigative work redefined broadcast journalism. Conrado de Quiros, whose essays blended intellect, wit, and social critique. Ricardo Puno Jr., Jose Taruc, Jarius Bondoc, Howie Severino, Rey Langit, and many others whose work left indelible marks on the profession.
These Hall of Fame honorees represent more than personal achievement.
They embody journalism's highest ideals.
The Provinces Speak
One of the most admirable aspects of the Journalism Awards has been its recognition that journalism's most important work is often performed far from the nation's capital.
Provincial newspapers, community broadcasters, and regional journalists have long played critical roles in informing citizens, exposing local issues, and fostering civic engagement.
The Awards consistently recognized these contributions.
Publications from Cebu, Davao, Baguio, Bacolod, Cagayan de Oro, Zamboanga, and numerous other regions received recognition alongside national media institutions.
This commitment reflected an understanding that democracy is strongest when citizens are informed not only about national affairs but also about the realities affecting their own communities.
The Journalism Awards became one of the few national programs to consistently celebrate excellence in regional journalism.
Journalism in Service of Democracy
The true significance of the Journalism Awards lies not in trophies, ceremonies, or citations.
It lies in the values they affrm.

At their core, the Awards recognize journalism as an essential pillar of democratic society. Every honored reporter, broadcaster, editor, publisher, photographer, or commentator contributes to a larger mission: enabling citizens to make informed decisions.

Investigative reporting promotes accountability.
Editorial commentary stimulates public debate.
Community journalism strengthens governance.
Documentary storytelling preserves collective memory.
Broadcast journalism brings information to millions.
Together, these functions fortn the foundation of an informed citizenry.
The Journalism Awards celebrate not merely professional competence but civic contribution.
Pro Patria: For Country
In 2021, under the Chairmanship of Dean Amado "Amading" Valdez, the Journalism Awards acquired a name that perfectly captured their deeper purpose.
The title Pro Patria Journalism Awards was suggested by veteran journalist, publisher, commentator, and fellow Rotarian Antonio Tony" Lopez, one of country's most accomplished media practitioners.
The phrase means "For Country."
Its adoption transformed the Awards into something larger than a recognition program.
It articulated a philosophy.

The title acknowledges that journalism, at its highest level, is an act of service. The pursuit of truth is not undertaken solely for professional advancement or institutional prestige. It is undertaken for the benefit of society itself.
Every journalist honored under the Pro Patria banner has contributed to the nation's understanding of itself.
They have informed public debate, challenged complacency, exposed wrongdoing. and strengthened democratic institutions.
In doing so, they have served their country.
The Awards in the Digital Age
The twenty-first century has introduced unprecedented challenges to journalism.
The rise of social media, misinformation, disinformation, artificial intelligence, and declining public trust has complicated the profession in ways earlier generations could scarcely have imagined.
Yet these challenges have also underscored the continuing relevance of the Journalism Awards.

At a time when facts are increasingly contested and information moves instantaneously across digital networks, the need for ethical, accurate, and responsible journalism has become more important than ever.
The Awards continue to evolve alongside the profession while remaining rooted in timeless principles of truth, fairness, accountability, and public service.
The Rotary Club of Manila and the Defense of Truth
The Journalism Awards stand as one of the clearest expressions of the Rotary Club of Manila's belief that civic leadership extends beyond philanthropy.
For decades, the Club has demonstrated that strengthening democratic institutions is itself a form of service.

By recognizing journalists, the Rotary Club of Manila affirms the importance of transparency, accountability, informed citizenship, and public discourse. It acknowledges that a society cannot address its challenges effectively unless its citizens have access to accurate and trustworthy information.
The Journalism Awards therefore represent more than support for media.
They represent support for democracy itself.
The Legacy Continues
Today, nearly sixty years after the first Journalism Awards were presented, the iconic quill continues to symbolize a noble and necessary profession.
Generations of journalists have received its recognition. Newspapers have risen and fallen. Technologies have changed. Political eras have come and gone.
Yet the principles underlying the Awards remain remarkably constant.

Truth remains essential.
Freedom remains precious.
Journalism remains indispensable.

The Rotary Club of Manila's Pro Patria Journalism Awards endure because they speak to these timeless realities. They remind us that societies progress when facts prevail over falsehoods, when accountability triumphs over secrecy, and when citizens are empowered by knowledge rather than deprived of it.
As long as journalists continue to pursue truth and serve the public, the quill will remain raised.

And as long as the Rotary Club of Manila continues to champion those ideals, the Pro Patria Journalism Awards will remain one of the country's most meaningful tributes to journalism in the service of nation, democracy, and freedom.

Pro Patria.
For Country.
For Truth.
For Generations Yet to Come.

body.text: THIS year's Journalism Pro Patria Honorees represent the very best of Philippine journalism. Through decades of dedication, courage, integrity, and excellence, they have not only chronicled history but helped shape it. Their careers stand as enduring reminders that journalism, at its finest, is more than a profession — it is a public trust and a service to country.
The Rotary Club of Manila proudly pays tribute to these distinguished media leaders whose legacy continues to inspire the profession and the nation they have faithfully served.

ELIMOTOUR
Vlogger of the Year

In an era where information travels at the speed of a click and audiences increasingly turn to digital platforms for news, insights, and inspiration, ELIMOTOUR has distinguished itself as a pioneering force in Filipino digital storytelling. More than a travel vlogger, ELIMOTOUR has become a cultural ambassador, educator, and chronicler of experiences, bringing audiences closer to the people, places, and stories that define the richness of the Philippines and the wider world.

Through compelling visuals, thoughtful narration, and a remarkable ability to connect with viewers, ELIMOTOUR has transformed travel content into a meaningful journalistic endeavor. His work goes beyond showcasing destinations. It documents local traditions, celebrates cultural heritage, highlights community initiatives, and fosters a deeper appreciation for the diversity that shapes the Filipino identity. Every episode reflects meticulous preparation, authenticity, and an unwavering commitment to presenting truthful and engaging content.

In a digital landscape often dominated by fleeting trends and superficial entertainment, ELIMOTOUR has consistently demonstrated that online platforms can be powerful tools for education, cultural understanding, and public engagement. His influence has encouraged responsible tourism, inspired countless viewers to explore and appreciate their own country, and provided exposure to local communities that might otherwise remain unseen.

For elevating digital content creation into a platform for learning and discovery; for exemplifying integrity, creativity, and excellence in online storytelling; and for inspiring audiences through meaningful and impactful narratives, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly confers upon ELIMOTOUR the Journalism Award for Vlogger of the Year.

BOMBO RADYO
Radio Station of the Year

For generations of Filipinos, Bombo Radyo has been more than a radio station — it has been a trusted companion, a reliable source of information, and a steadfast guardian of public interest. Through decades of dedicated service, Bombo Radyo has built an enduring legacy founded upon journalistic integrity, community engagement, and an unwavering commitment to truth.

Its extensive network has enabled it to reach urban centers and remote communities alike, ensuring that timely news, public affairs discussions, and critical information remain accessible to millions of listeners throughout the country. Whether reporting on national developments, local concerns, natural disasters, or matters of public safety, Bombo Radyo has consistently demonstrated the essential role of radio as a lifeline of information and a pillar of democracy.

What distinguishes Bombo Radyo is its deep connection to the communities it serves. Its broadcasters and reporters understand the pulse of the nation because they remain close to the people whose stories they tell. This commitment to grassroots journalism has fostered trust among audiences and reinforced the station's reputation as one of the country's most credible and influential broadcast institutions.

In a rapidly evolving media environment, Bombo Radyo has successfully adapted to new technologies while preserving the core values that have guided its mission for decades. Its dedication to public set-vice, factual reporting, and civic responsibility continues to set a standard for excellence in Philippine broadcasting.

For its outstanding contribution to radio journalism, its steadfast commitment to informing and empowering the Filipino people, and its enduring legacy of public service, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly honors Bombo Radyo as Radio Station of the Year.

ANGELO B. PALMONES
Radio Personality of the Year

Throughout a distinguished career in broadcasting and public communication, Angelo Palmones has demonstrated how journalism can serve as a bridge between knowledge and society. As a respected broadcaster, educator, and advocate for science and evidence-based discourse, he has consistently elevated the quality of public conversation through insightful reporting and responsible communication.

Known for his intellectual rigor and clarity of expression, Palmones possesses the rare ability to translate complex scientific, technological, and public policy issues into language that resonates with ordinary Citizens. His work has empowered audiences to better understand the challenges and opportunities facing society, enabling them to make more informed decisions as citizens and stakeholders in nation-building.

Beyond his accomplishments as a broadcaster, he has championed the values of critical thinking, factual accuracy, and public accountability. In an age where misinformation and sensationalism often threaten informed discourse, Angelo Palmones has remained steadfast in his commitment to truth and responsible journalism. His professionalism, credibility, and dedication to public education have earned him the respect of colleagues and listeners alike.

His contributions exemplify the enduring power of radio as a platform for enlightenment and civic engagement. Through every broadcast, he has demonstrated that journalism is not merely about reporting events but about helping citizens understand their significance and implications.

For his exceptional contributions to radio broadcasting, his dedication to public education, and his steadfast commitment to responsible journalism, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly presents Angelo Palmones with the Journalism Award for Radio Personality of the Year.

GMA Network
Television Station of the Year

For more than seven decades, GMA Network has stood as one of the Philippines' most respected and influential media institutions. Through its commitment to journalistic excellence, technological innovation, and public sew-ice, it has become a trusted source of information for millions of Filipinos both at home and abroad.

At the heart of GMA Network's success lies its unwavering dedication to delivering accurate, balanced, and timely news. Its journalists, producers, and media professionals have consistently demonstrated courage and professionalism in covering events of national significance, often under challenging circumstances. From elections and natural disasters to social issues and international developments, GMA Network has provided audiences with comprehensive coverage grounded in the principles of fairness and truth.

Beyond news reporting, GMA Network has continuously expanded the boundaries of broadcast journalism through innovative programming, investigative reporting, and public affairs initiatives that encourage informed public discourse. Its commitment to leveraging technology has allowed it to reach audiences across multiple platforms, ensuring that credible information remains accessible in an increasingly digital world.

Throughout its history, GMA Network has upheld the essential role of a free and responsible press in strengthening democratic institutions and empowering citizens. Its contributions have helped shape national conversations, promote accountability, and foster a better-informed society.
For its enduring commitment to journalistic excellence, public service, and innovation in broadcasting, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly recognizes GMA Network as Television Station of the Year.

ALFONSO TOMAS P. ARAULLO
TV Journalist of the Year

Among the most respected journalists of his generation, Atom Araullo has distinguished himself through courage, compassion, and an unwavering commitment to telling stories that matter. Throughout his career, he has consistently brought viewers beyond the headlines and into the lives of individuals and communities whose experiences illuminate the most pressing issues of our time.

Renowned for his immersive reporting and investigative journalism, Araullo has covered natural disasters, humanitarian crises, environmental challenges, social inequalities, and stories of resilience across the Philippines and around the world. His work reflects a profound understanding that journalism is ultimately about people — their struggles, aspirations, and dignity.

What sets Atom Araullo apart is his ability to combine meticulous reporting with genuine empathy. He approaches every assignment with intellectual rigor and human sensitivity, ensuring that complex issues are presented with both accuracy and context. Through his reporting, audiences gain not only information but a Iso a deeper appreciation of the realities faced by fellow citizens.

In an era marked by rapid information flows and increasing public skepticism, Atom Araullo has remained a steadfast advocate for truth, accountability, and responsible journalism. His work embodies the highest ideals of the profession and serves as an inspiration to aspiring journalists across the nation.

For his exceptional achievements in television journalism, his fearless pursuit of truth, and his enduring commitment to public service through story telling. the Rotary Club of Manila proudly confers upon Atom Araullo the Journalism Award for TV Journalist of the Year.

BUSINESSMIRROR
Newspaper of the Year

Since its founding, BusinessMirror has earned a distinguished reputation as one of the country's most credible and insightful newspapers. While widely recognized for its comprehensive coverage of business and economic affairs. it has also established itself as a trusted Source Of reporting on governance, public policy, environment, agriculture, education, and social development.

At a time when economic decisions increasingly influence the lives of ordinary citizens, BusinessMirror has played a vital role in helping readers understand the forces shaping the nation's future. Through balanced reporting, thoughtful analysis, and rigorous editorial standards, it has provided clarity on complex issues that affect businesses, government institutions, and communities alike.

Its journalists and editors have consistently demonstrated a commitment to independence, and public accountability. By presenting facts within their broader social and economic contexts, BusinessMirror has enriched public discourse and empowered readers to engage more meaningfully with issues of national importance.

Beyond reporting events, BusinessMirror contributes to nation-building by fostering informed decision-making among policymakers, business leaders, and citizens. Its dedication to excellence reflects the essential role of quality journalism in promoting transparency, economic progress, and democratic participation.

For its outstanding contributions to Philippine journalism, its commitment to informing and enlightening the public, and its consistent pursuit of editorial excellence, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly honors BusinessMirror as Newspaper of the Year.

JARIUS Y. BONDOC
Opinion Writer of the Year

For decades, Jarius Bondoc has stood among the most respected voices in Philippine opinion journalism. Through incisive commentary, fearless analysis, and an unwavering commitment to accountability, he has consistently challenged institutions, exposed wrongdoing, and advocated for the public interest.

His columns are distinguished not merely by eloquence but by substance. Combining investigative rigor with thoughtful interpretation, Bondoc has demonstrated how opinion writing can serve as a powerful instrument for transparency, reform, and civic engagement. His work reflects a deep understanding of governance, public policy, and the issues that affect the lives of ordinary Filipinos.

Throughout his distinguished career, he has shown remarkable courage in addressing controversial topics and holding those in positions of power accountable. At a time when independent voices remain essential to the health of democratic societies, Jarius Bondoc has exemplified the vital role of opinion journalism in fostering informed debate and encouraging responsible governance.

His writings continue to influence public discourse and inspire both readers and fellow journalists to value truth, integrity, and intellectual honesty. Through his persistent pursuit of facts and justice, he has reinforced the public's faith in journalism as a force for positive change.

For his distinguished career, his outstanding contribution to public discourse, and his steadfast dedication to truth and accountability, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly presents Jarius Bondoc with the Journalism Award for Opinion Writer of the Year.

CHRISTIAN V. ESGUERRA
Online Individual Journalist of the Year

As journalism continues to evolve in the digital age, Christian Esguerra has emerged as one of the Philippines' most respected and influential online journalists. Through his widely followed platform, Facts First, he has demonstrated that digital media can serve not only as a source of information but also as a venue for meaningful dialogue, critical analysis, and civic engagement.

Esguerra has earned the trust of audiences through his unwavering commitment to factual reporting, thoughtful interviews, and evidence-based commentary. In an environment increasingly challenged by misinformation, polarization, and declining public trust, he has consistently upheld the fundamental principles of journalism— accuracy, fairness, independence, and accountability.

His interviews bring together policymakers, experts, thought leaders, and stakeholders to discuss issues of national significance with depth and clarity. By encouraging informed discussion rather than sensationalism, he has elevated the quality of public discourse and empowered citizens to engage more thoughtfully with the issues shaping their communities and the nation.

Christian Esguerra's work exemplifies how journalists can adapt to new platforms without compromising professional standards. His dedication to truth and public service demonstrates that credible journalism remains indispensable regardless of the medium through which it is delivered.

For his exemplary achievements in online journalism, his commitment to factual and responsible reporting, and his invaluable contribution to an informed and engaged citizenry, the Rotary Club of Manila proudly honors Christian Esguerra as Online Individual Journalist of the Year.

IN every generation, societies are ultimately shaped by the quality of the information upon which their citizens act.

Governments make decisions.
Businesses allocate capital.
Communities respond to crises.
Families form opinions.
Democracies elect leaders.
Yet all these depend upon one indispensable foundation: truth.
That is why journalism matters.

For nearly six decades, the Rotary Club of Manila Journalism Awards have stood as one of the nation's most enduring tributes to those who dedicate their lives to seeking, verifying, and communicating the truth. Long before social media transformed the information landscape, long before algorithms amplified voices both credible and questionable, the Rotary Club of Manila recognized that a free and responsible press is essential to a free and responsible society.
Today, that conviction is more relevant than ever.

We live in an age of unprecedented connectivity. Information travels across continents in seconds. News breaks instantly. Opinions spread virally. Artificial intelligence generates content at remarkable speed. Yet amid this abundance of information lies a growing challenge: distinguishing fact from fiction, evidence from speculation, and journalism from mere noise.
The role of the journalist has therefore become not less important, but more important than ever.

A journalist's task is not simply to report events. It is to provide context amid confusion, clarity amid complexity, and accountability amid power. It requires courage to ask difficult questions, discipline to verify facts, integrity to resist pressure, and humility to place truth above personal preference.
The finest journalists serve not political interests, commercial interests, or ideological interests. They serve the public interest.

That commitment has often come at considerable personal cost. Throughout history, journalists have faced intimidation, censorship, threats, and even violence. Yet many have persevered because they understood that silence in the face of falsehood is not neutrality—it is surrender.
The Rotary Club of Manila Journalism Awards were established to honor precisely this spirit.

Over the decades, the awards have recognized some of the most respected names in Philippine media—men and women whose work informed the nation, challenged complacency, exposed wrongdoing, elevated public discourse, and inspired future generations of journalists. Their achievements remind us that journalism, at its best, is a public service.
The Journalism Awards are therefore more than a recognition program. They are a statement of values.
They affirm that truth matters.
They affirm that facts matter.
They affirm that responsible journalism remains indispensable to national development, good governance, and democratic progress.

As Rotary's theme this year calls upon us to Unite for Good, we recognize that meaningful unity cannot be built upon misinformation, division, or ignorance. Genuine progress requires informed citizens capable of making thoughtful decisions. It requires institutions committed to transparency. It requires journalists who continue to illuminate issues that affect the lives of millions.
The Rotary Club of Manila salutes all those who have devoted their talents, intellect, and courage to this noble profession.
May they continue to remind us that while technology changes, platforms evolve, and headlines fade, the pursuit of truth remains timeless.
For in the end, societies flourish not merely because they are prosperous, but because they are informed.
And informed societies are built by journalists who have the courage to tell the truth.

body.text: President's Message

TODAY, the Rotary Club Of Manila proudly celebrates one Of its most cherished and enduring signature projects — the Pro Patria Journalism Awards. It is especially fitting that we gather today on the eve of our nation's celebration of independence. As the Philippines marks another year of freedom and nationhood, we are reminded that a truly independent nation is sustained not only by brave heroes of the past, but also by courageous voices of the present – journalists who speak truth to power, give voice to the people, and safeguard the public's right to know.

In every democratic society, journalism occupies a sacred space between power and the people. It informs citizens, shapes public discourse, exposes wrongdoing, and preserves truth against distortion. Yet journalism is not merely about reporting events or chasing headlines. At its highest form, journalism is an act of patriotism. Indeed, pro-patria and responsible journalism are synonymous. They go hand in hand because both are ultimately anchored on a common purpose: the welfare and advancement of the nation.

To be pro-patria means to act for the good of one's country. It is a commitment to uphold national interests, protect democratic institutions, and strengthen the moral and civic foundations of society. Responsible journalism pursues exactly the same objectives.
It seeks truth not to destroy, but to enlighten; not to divide, but to guide society toward justice, accountability, and progress.

A responsible journalist understands that the power of the press carries enormous influence. Words can inspire unity or provoke discord. News can educate citizens or manipulate public opinion. In an era dominated by misinformation, sensationalism, and digital noise, the duty of journalists has become even more critical. Patriotism in journalism does not mean blind loyalty to government or the suppression of criticism. On the contrary, genuine love of country requires courage to speak truth to power when necessary. It demands vigilance against corruption, abuse, and incompetence because these weaken the nation from within.

History has repeatedly shown that nations flourish when journalism remains principled and responsible. Investigative reporting has uncovered corruption, defended human rights, and amplified the voices of the marginalized. Journalists who expose wrongdoing often do so not out of hostility toward their country, but out of profound belief that the nation deserves better leadership, better governance, and better institutions. In this sense, responsible journalism becomes an indispensable pillar of nation-building.

At the same time, patriotism imposes discipline upon the practice of journalism. Responsible journalists verify facts before publication, avoid reckless accusations, and reject sensationalism designed solely for profit or popularity. They understand that false information can erode public trust, inflame social tensions, and damage democratic stability. A journalist who deliberately spreads misinformation in pursuit of ratings or influence cannot claim to serve the country. National interest is never advanced by deception.

Responsible journalism also nurtures informed citizenship. Democracies thrive when citizens are equipped with accurate information and thoughtful analysis. Through ethical reporting, journalists empower people to participate meaningfully in public life. make sound decisions, and hold leaders accountable. In this way, journalism strengthens democracy itself — one of the highest expressions of patriotism.

Ultimately, pro-patria and responsible journalism are inseparable because both seek truth, justice, accountability, and the common good. They are not opposing ideals, but complementary duties. A journalist who genuinely loves country serves the people with honesty, fairness, courage, and integrity. And a nation that values patriotism must equally value a free, ethical, and responsible press.

As the head of Finasiatech Corpora-tion, he has been instrumental in advancing e-mobility initiatives that provide electric vehicle solutions for TODA drivers, promoting both sustainability and inclusive growth. A dynamic professional and community leader, Mr. Pangilinan continues to create meaningful impact across industries.
