PRES. RAOUL C. CREENCIA 35th Weekly Membership Meeting Editorial  Reginald T. Yu Editor-in-Chief AT first glance, the RCManila Foundation, Inc. (RCMFI) may appear to be simply the fundraising arm of the Rotary Club of Manila. That description is accurate — but incomplete. Fundraising, after all, is not the mission.
It is merely the means.
The mission is service. And in Rotary, service is ultimately measured not by how much money is raised but by how many lives are transformed. This reality came into sharper focus during the recent RCMFI Day and Year-End Report, where members reflected on the Foundation’s accomplishments and listened to the Classification Talk of Manuel E. “AJ” Pangilinan, Chief Executive Officer of Finasiatech Corp. Together, the presentations highlighted an essential truth: organizations exist not merely to sustain themselves but to create impact beyond themselves. That principle applies equally to businesses, charities, foundations, and Rotary clubs. For more than a century, the Rotary Club of Manila has carried out projects that have touched countless lives. Yet even the noblest ideas require resources. Medical missions require medicines. Educational programs require materials. Disaster response requires logistics. Community development requires funding. Good intentions alone do not build schools, restore sight, feed children, or rebuild communities after calamities. Execution does.
And execution requires resources.
That is where RCMFI enters the picture. As the official foundation of the Rotary Club of Manila, RCMFI serves as the vehicle through which generosity is transformed into tangible and measurable service. It allows members, donors, partners, and benefactors to convert goodwill into action and compassion into results. Too often, fundraising is viewed as a necessary inconvenience—something organizations must do before they can pursue their real work. That mindset misunderstands the nature of philanthropy. Fundraising is not asking people to give away money. Fundraising is inviting people to participate in a mission larger than themselves. Every peso donated represents a vote of confidence in a cause. It reflects trust that the resources entrusted to the Foundation will be used wisely, transparently, and effectively to improve lives. In that sense, fundraising is not primarily a financial activity. It is a moral activity. It is the process of connecting resources with needs, generosity with opportunity, and success with responsibility. This has become especially important in a society where the gap between need and available resources often appears overwhelming. The challenges facing the Philippines are immense. Millions remain vulnerable to poverty.
Children continue to suffer from malnutrition.
Communities remain exposed to natural disasters.
Schools struggle with shortages.
Healthcare remains inaccessible for many families.
Government cannot solve these problems alone. Neither can the private sector. Nor can civil society organizations working independently. Meaningful change requires partnerships. It requires institutions capable of mobilizing resources, building trust, and translating collective goodwill into effective action. That is precisely the role foundations such as RCMFI play. The most successful foundations understand that their greatest asset is not money. It is credibility. Money can be raised.
Credibility must be earned. Every successful project completed, every beneficiary served, every donor properly accounted for, and every promise fulfilled strengthens the trust upon which future service depends. This is why governance matters.
Transparency matters.
Accountability matters. Without them, fundraising becomes solicitation. With them, fundraising becomes stewardship. The recent accomplishments reported by RCMFI demonstrate what can happen when stewardship is practiced well. Through the support of members, partners, and benefactors, the Foundation has continued to expand the Rotary Club of Manila’s capacity to serve communities and respond to emerging needs. Yet perhaps the most important lesson from RCMFI Day is that service organizations must never become complacent. Success creates new responsibilities. The more effective an institution becomes, the greater the expectations placed upon it. The challenge is not merely to maintain momentum but to scale impact. How can more children be reached?
How can more communities be served?
How can partnerships be expanded?
How can donor confidence be strengthened?
How can every peso entrusted to the Foundation create the greatest possible good? These questions should guide the future of RCMFI. The Classification Talk by AJ Pangilinan offers a complementary perspective. Every profession, every enterprise, and every organization ultimately exists to create value beyond itself. Businesses create jobs. Entrepreneurs create opportunities. Institutions create platforms through which individuals can contribute to society. Foundations perform a similar role. They convert individual generosity into collective action. They transform isolated acts of kindness into organized programs capable of creating lasting change. That is why RCMFI deserves recognition not merely as the fundraising arm of the Rotary Club of Manila, but as one of its most important instruments of service. Its significance lies not in the funds it raises but in what those funds make possible. A child fed.
A student educated.
A patient treated.
A family assisted.
A community rebuilt.
A life transformed. These are the true metrics of success. In the final analysis, RCMFI exists because Rotary’s vision extends beyond fellowship. It extends beyond meetings.
It extends even beyond the Club itself. Its purpose is to ensure that the generosity, expertise, and leadership of Rotarians become a force for lasting good in society. Fundraising is simply how the journey begins. Service is where it ends. And that is why RCMFI matters more than ever. RC Manila Foundation: Stewarding Resources, Sustaining Service  President's Message AS I prepare to assume the chairmanship of the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation, Inc. (RCMFI) on 1 July, it is both fitting and meaningful that today’s meeting is devoted to the Foundation’s Annual Report. More than a routine presentation, this occasion provides an important opportunity for the membership of the Rotary Club of Manila -- and particularly the members of the Foundation -- to gain a deeper appreciation of the work being undertaken by the organization that serves as the financial backbone of many of the Club’s service initiatives. The RCM Foundation occupies a unique and indispensable role within our institution. While the Club itself conceives and implements projects that respond to the needs of our communities, the Foundation helps ensure that these worthy endeavors have the resources necessary to succeed. Through prudent stewardship, sound financial management, and strategic support, the Foundation transforms generosity into meaningful and lasting impact. Today, we recognize the accomplishments of the current officers and trustees of the Foundation, led by Chairman and Past District Governor Alex Cureg. Under their leadership, the Foundation has continued to fulfill its mandate with diligence and integrity. Their efforts have strengthened the Foundation’s capacity to support the Club’s various programs while safeguarding its assets for future generations of Rotarians. The projects supported by the Foundation during the past year reflect Rotary’s enduring commitment to service above self. From educational and humanitarian initiatives to community development programs, the Foundation has played a vital role in enabling the Club to translate its vision into action. These projects have touched lives, created opportunities, and reinforced RCM’s reputation as a force for positive change. Equally noteworthy are the ongoing preparations for the 4th RCM Cup on June 22, which has become RCMFI’s most significant yearly fund mobilization activity. The dedication and hard work invested in organizing this event demonstrate the Foundation’s commitment not only to fundraising but also to building partnerships, promoting fellowship, and expanding the Club’s capacity to serve. As final preparations move into high gear, the enthusiasm and cooperation of all those involved are deserving of recognition and appreciation. As we review the Foundation’s achievements over the past year, we do so with profound gratitude for the officers, trustees, donors, and volunteers whose dedication and commitment have enabled the Foundation to fulfill its mission. Their collective efforts have ensured that the resources entrusted to the Foundation were managed responsibly and directed toward projects that advance RCM’s enduring commitment to service. Every scholarship granted, every community initiative supported, and all programs successfully implemented this Rotary year stand as a testament to their hard work and faithful stewardship. At the same time, we look to the future with optimism and confidence. The challenges confronting our communities continue to evolve, bringing with them new opportunities for Rotary to make a meaningful difference. As the service projects of the Club become more ambitious and far-reaching, the role of the Foundation becomes even more critical. Beyond providing financial support, RCMFI serves as a trusted platform through which the generosity of Rotarians and friends of Rotary is transformed into tangible and lasting impact. It is the bridge that connects resources with purpose, and goodwill with action. The strength of RCM has always rested upon the willingness of its members to contribute not only their financial resources, but also their time, expertise, leadership, and passion in pursuit of a greater purpose. For more than a century, generations of Manila Rotarians have demonstrated that when individuals unite behind a common vision of service, extraordinary things can be accomplished. RCMFI remains a vital instrument in sustaining that tradition, ensuring that the Club possesses the capacity and stability necessary to carry out its mission for years to come. As we embark on another Rotary year, let us reaffirm our commitment to strengthening the Foundation and expanding its ability to support projects that uplift lives and strengthen communities. Let us continue to cultivate a culture of generosity, accountability, and stewardship worthy of the trust placed in us by our members, partners, and beneficiaries. Together, we will build upon the solid foundation laid by those who came before us, preserving their legacy while creating new opportunities to serve. In doing so, we honor not only the achievements of the past year but also the enduring ideals of Rotary itself. Together, we will continue to build on this legacy of stewardship, service, and impact, ensuring that RCMFI remains a powerful force for good for the communities we serve today and for the generations that will follow. Pro Patria 2026: Honoring Journalists Who Keep the Nation Free PE Reginald T. Yu AS the nation marked its 128 Indepen- dence Day, the Rotary Club of Manila gathered leaders from media, government, business, the judiciary, and civil society for one of its most meaningful annual traditions: the Pro Patria Journalism Awards 2026. Held at the Fairmont Hotel Makati during the Club’s 34th Weekly Membership Meeting, the ceremony celebrated journalists, broadcasters, media organizations, and digital storytellers whose work has advanced truth, accountability, patriotism, and public service. More than an awards program, the event served as a reaffirmation of the indispensable role that a free and responsible press plays in safeguarding democracy and strengthening the nation. The evening opened with a stirring Parade of Colors led by the Philippine Coast Guard, followed by the Doxology, the Philippine National Anthem, and the Rotary Club of Manila Hymn. Rotary Club of Manila President Atty. Raoul C. Creencia formally called the meeting to order and welcomed members and guests to a celebration that linked the ideals of Philippine independence with the enduring mission of journalism. The President’s Message: Freedom Requires Truth In his welcome remarks and Independence Day toast, President Creencia reminded the gathering that freedom is sustained not only by those who fought for it on the battlefield, but also by those who continue to defend it through the pursuit of truth. By hosting the Pro Patria Journalism Awards as part of its Independence Day celebration, the Rotary Club of Manila reaffirmed its belief that journalism remains one of the strongest pillars of a democratic society. The evening paid tribute to media practitioners who continue to serve the public interest with courage, integrity, and profession alism amid increasing challenges to truth and public discourse. The Chairman’s Message: Journalism as Patriotism The evening’s most reflective address came from Past Director Amado “Amading” Valdez, Chairman of the Pro Patria Journalism Awards. Valdez recounted how the Rotary Club of Manila decided several years ago to rename the awards “Pro Patria”—Latin for “For Country”— during the presidency of Hermie Esguerra. The decision emerged from a desire to create an Independence Day tradition that would celebrate not only freedom but also those who help preserve it through journalism. Drawing from the example of the Daily Tribune, which prominently displays its previous Pro Patria award on its masthead, Valdez underscored what the recognition represents: journalism practiced “without fear and without favor.” He described journalism as a form of storytelling that transcends mere narration. At its highest level, journalism creates history. It gives meaning to events, shapes public memory, and provides future generations with an understanding of their time. “Journalism,” he observed, “is storytelling with a special purpose.” Yet for Valdez, technical skill alone is insufficient. The defining quality of great journalists is courage—the willingness to take risks in pursuit of truth, integrity, and hope. He noted that this common thread united all the evening’s honorees. Whether working in traditional media or digital platforms, they demonstrated a commitment to country that went beyond professional achievement. Their work reflected a willingness to confront difficult truths and to place public service above personal comfort. In one of the evening’s most moving moments, Valdez shared how, after the passing of his wife, he found renewed optimism and love for the Philippines through travel vlogs that rediscovered the beauty of Northern Luzon. That personal experience ultimately inspired the recognition of the evening’s Vlogger of the Year and underscored the broader message of the awards: journalism and storytelling can deepen our appreciation of country and rekindle hope in difficult times. The 2026 Pro Patria Journalism Awardees The Rotary Club of Manila recognized eight outstanding recipients whose work exemplifies the highest standards of journalism and public communication. Eleazar D. Caldona (Elimotour) - Vlogger of the Year Through authentic motorcycle journeys into remote communities and hidden destinations across Northern Luzon and the Cordilleras, Elimotour has introduced Filipinos to the country’s natural beauty, cultural richness, and resilient communities. The award citation praised his raw and honest storytelling, which enables viewers to experience the challenges, triumphs, and wonder of exploration alongside him. His work encourages viewers to rediscover the Philippines and strengthens appreciation for the nation’s heritage. Bombo Radyo - Radio Station of the Year For decades, Bombo Radyo has remained one of the country’s most trusted sources of news and public service information. The citation highlighted its extensive provincial reach, disaster coverage, and community-centered programming that has consistently informed and protected Filipinos during emergencies and crises. Its reputation for public service and meaningful broadcasting has made it a pillar of responsible journalism. Christian V. Esguerra - Most Outstanding Online Journalist of the Year Christian Esguerra was honored for elevating public discourse through responsible and impactful digital journalism. His work promotes truth, accountability, democratic engagement, and critical thinking. Through digital platforms, interviews, and analysis, he has become one of the country's most influential voices in contemporary journalism. Angelo Palmones - Radio Broadcaster of the Year A respected veteran broadcaster, Angelo Palmones was recognized for sustaining excellence in radio journalism while preserving the relevance and dignity of the medium. His work embodies integrity, ethical journalism, and faithful service to country—values central to the spirit of the Pro Patria Awards. Business Mirror - Newspaper of the Year BusinessMirror received recognition for its unwavering commitment to development oriented journalism. Its extensive coverage of business, infrastructure, agriculture, energy, public policy, and economic development has made it an indispensable source of information for both public and private sector leaders. The newspaper was cited for contributing meaningfully to economic understanding and nation-building. Jarius Ymzon Bondoc - Opinion Writer of the Year Through his long-running “Gotcha” column and decades of investigative commentary, Jarius Bondoc has consistently promoted accountability, exposed corruption, and stimulated informed public discourse. The citation recognized his analytical depth, moral courage, and dedication to public service. GMA Network - Television Station of the Year GMA Network was honored for delivering some of the country's most comprehensive and credible news and documentary programming. The citation specifically highlighted its investigative reporting and documentary work, including the internationally acclaimed POGOLAND documentary and its groundbreaking coverage of the flood-control controversy that brought governance issues into national focus. Alfonso Tomas "Atom" Pagaduan Araullo - Television Journalist of the Year One of the country's most respected journalists and documentarians, Atom Araullo was recognized for his investigative work through The Atom Araullo Specials: POGOLAND. The documentary received major international recognition while also contributing to meaningful policy discussions and public awareness regarding governance and law enforcement issues. Voices of Integrity: The Acceptance Speeches The awardees’ acceptance speeches revealed a common theme: journalism remains both a privilege and a responsibility. Elimotour: Sharing the Beauty of the Philippines Receiving the Vlogger of the Year Award, Eleazar Caldona expressed surprise and gratitude for the recognition. He explained that he began creating content simply to share adventures in remote and little-known destinations. For him, the award was not merely a recognition of his channel but also a tribute to the beauty, culture, and history of Northern Luzon and the Cordilleras. He pledged to continue telling the stories of the country with pride and love for the nation. Angelo Palmones: A Beacon of Hope Angelo Palmones kept his remarks characteristically brief and humorous, joking about the reputation of journalists for delivering long speeches. BusinessMirror: Pro-Development Journalism Accepting the Newspaper of the Year Award, BusinessMirror reaffirmed its editorial philosophy of being “pro-development, pro business, and pro-government” while remaining committed to fact based reporting. Its representative emphasized that despite the many challenges confronting the Philippines, immense opportunities remain. The newspaper's mission, he said, is to help citizens recognize those opportunities while remaining grounded in verified facts and responsible journalism. Jarius Bondoc: Patriotism as Inheritance Jarius Bondoc delivered perhaps the evening’s most eloquent and patriotic acceptance speech. He dedicated the award to his wife, daughter, and longtime assistant before reflecting on the importance of passing patriotism to future generations. Drawing from Andres Bonifacio’s poem Pag-ibig sa Tinubuang Lupa, he reminded the audience that love of country remains among the highest virtues citizens can leave behind. His speech underscored the connection between journalism and citizenship. GMA Network: Journalism as a Democratic Institution Accepting on behalf of GMA Network, Vice President Michelle Seva emphasized that the recognition belonged not only to the network but also to the thousands of journalists and media professionals who serve audiences every day. She observed that recent events have demonstrated how interconnected societies have become and why trustworthy information remains essential. She stressed that democracy is strongest when citizens have access to facts they can trust and affirmed GMA's commitment to fair, responsible, and independent journalism. Atom Araullo: Following the Evidence Atom Araullo reflected on the increasingly difficult environment confronting journalists. At a time when facts are challenged and misinformation proliferates, he emphasized that the journalist’s duty remains unchanged: to ask questions, follow evidence wherever it leads, and ensure that ordinary voices are heard. He accepted the award on behalf of the reporters, researchers, producers, editors, camera operators, and news workers who contribute to investigative journalism, recognizing journalism as a collective endeavor. Christian Esguerra: Credibility in the Digital Age Christian Esguerra delivered one of the evening’s most thought provoking speeches. He noted that in today’s digital environment, almost everyone can become a content creator. Yet being believable is not the same as being credible. Credibility, he argued, is earned through years of disciplined work, adherence to ethical standards, and commitment to truth. Awards such as the Pro Patria recognition, he said, create an obligation to continually prove oneself worthy of public trust. His remarks served as a powerful reminder that integrity remains journalism’s most valuable asset. Journalism and the Republic The 2026 Pro Patria Journalism Awards concluded with a special musical performance by actress and singer Pinky Marquez before President Raoul Creencia delivered the response and formally adjourned the meeting. More importantly, however, the evening ended with a renewed appreciation for journalism’s role in nation-building. In honoring broadcasters, reporters, commentators, media organizations, and digital storytellers, the Rotary Club of Manila reaffirmed a principle that remains as relevant today as it was when the nation first won its independence: a free people require truthful information, courageous journalism, and citizens willing to place country above self. That is the enduring spirit of Pro Patria — For Country.

The recent accomplishments reported by RCMFI demonstrate what can happen when stewardship is practiced well. Through the support of members, partners, and benefactors, the Foundation has continued to expand the Rotary Club of Manila’s capacity to serve communities and respond to emerging needs.
Yet perhaps the most important lesson from RCMFI Day is that service organizations must never become complacent.
Success creates new responsibilities.
The more effective an institution becomes, the greater the expectations placed upon it.
The challenge is not merely to maintain momentum but to scale impact.

How can more children be reached?
How can more communities be served?
How can partnerships be expanded?
How can donor confidence be strengthened?
How can every peso entrusted to the Foundation create the greatest possible good?
These questions should guide the future of RCMFI.

The Classification Talk by AJ Pangilinan offers a complementary perspective. Every profession, every enterprise, and every organization ultimately exists to create value beyond itself. Businesses create jobs. Entrepreneurs create opportunities. Institutions create platforms through which individuals can contribute to society.
Foundations perform a similar role.
They convert individual generosity into collective action.
They transform isolated acts of kindness into organized programs capable of creating lasting change.
That is why RCMFI deserves recognition not merely as the fundraising arm of the Rotary Club of Manila, but as one of its most important instruments of service.
Its significance lies not in the funds it raises but in what those funds make possible.

A child fed.
A student educated.
A patient treated.
A family assisted.
A community rebuilt.
A life transformed.
These are the true metrics of success.
In the final analysis, RCMFI exists because Rotary’s vision extends beyond fellowship.

It extends beyond meetings.
It extends even beyond the Club itself.
Its purpose is to ensure that the generosity, expertise, and leadership of Rotarians become a force for lasting good in society.
Fundraising is simply how the journey begins.
Service is where it ends.
And that is why RCMFI matters more than ever.

body.text: President's Message

AS I prepare to assume the chairmanship of the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation, Inc. (RCMFI) on 1 July, it is both fitting and meaningful that today’s meeting is devoted to the Foundation’s Annual Report.

More than a routine presentation, this occasion provides an important opportunity for the membership of the Rotary Club of Manila -- and particularly the members of the Foundation -- to gain a deeper appreciation of the work being undertaken by the organization that serves as the financial backbone of many of the Club’s service initiatives.

The RCM Foundation occupies a unique and indispensable role within our institution. While the Club itself conceives and implements projects that respond to the needs of our communities, the Foundation helps ensure that these worthy endeavors have the resources necessary to succeed. Through prudent stewardship, sound financial management, and strategic support, the Foundation transforms generosity into meaningful and lasting impact.

Today, we recognize the accomplishments of the current officers and trustees of the Foundation, led by Chairman and Past District Governor Alex Cureg. Under their leadership, the Foundation has continued to fulfill its mandate with diligence and integrity. Their efforts have strengthened the Foundation’s capacity to support the Club’s various programs while safeguarding its assets for future generations of Rotarians.

The projects supported by the Foundation during the past year reflect Rotary’s enduring commitment to service above self. From educational and humanitarian initiatives to community development programs, the Foundation has played a vital role in enabling the Club to translate its vision into action. These projects have touched lives, created opportunities, and reinforced RCM’s reputation as a force for positive change.

Equally noteworthy are the ongoing preparations for the 4th RCM Cup on June 22, which has become RCMFI’s most significant yearly fund mobilization activity. The dedication and hard work invested in organizing this event demonstrate the Foundation’s commitment not only to fundraising but also to building partnerships, promoting fellowship, and expanding the Club’s capacity to serve. As final preparations move into high gear, the enthusiasm and cooperation of all those involved are deserving of recognition and appreciation.

As we review the Foundation’s achievements over the past year, we do so with profound gratitude for the officers, trustees, donors, and volunteers whose dedication and commitment have enabled the Foundation to fulfill its mission. Their collective efforts have ensured that the resources entrusted to the Foundation were managed responsibly and directed toward projects that advance RCM’s enduring commitment to service. Every scholarship granted, every community initiative supported, and all programs successfully implemented this Rotary year stand as a testament to their hard work and faithful stewardship.
At the same time, we look to the future with optimism and confidence.

The challenges confronting our communities continue to evolve, bringing with them new opportunities for Rotary to make a meaningful difference. As the service projects of the Club become more ambitious and far-reaching, the role of the Foundation becomes even more critical. Beyond providing financial support, RCMFI serves as a trusted platform through which the generosity of Rotarians and friends of Rotary is transformed into tangible and lasting impact. It is the bridge that connects resources with purpose, and goodwill with action.

The strength of RCM has always rested upon the willingness of its members to contribute not only their financial resources, but also their time, expertise, leadership, and passion in pursuit of a greater purpose. For more than a century, generations of Manila Rotarians have demonstrated that when individuals unite behind a common vision of service, extraordinary things can be accomplished. RCMFI remains a vital instrument in sustaining that tradition, ensuring that the Club possesses the capacity and stability necessary to carry out its mission for years to come.

As we embark on another Rotary year, let us reaffirm our commitment to strengthening the Foundation and expanding its ability to support projects that uplift lives and strengthen communities. Let us continue to cultivate a culture of generosity, accountability, and stewardship worthy of the trust placed in us by our members, partners, and beneficiaries.
Together, we will build upon the solid foundation laid by those who came before us, preserving their legacy while creating new opportunities to serve.

In doing so, we honor not only the achievements of the past year but also the enduring ideals of Rotary itself. Together, we will continue to build on this legacy of stewardship, service, and impact, ensuring that RCMFI remains a powerful force for good for the communities we serve today and for the generations that will follow.

articles.title: Pro Patria 2026: Honoring Journalists Who Keep the Nation Free

body.text: AS the nation marked its 128 Indepen- dence Day, the Rotary Club of Manila gathered leaders from media, government, business, the judiciary, and civil society for one of its most meaningful annual traditions: the Pro Patria Journalism Awards 2026.

Held at the Fairmont Hotel Makati during the Club’s 34th Weekly Membership Meeting, the ceremony celebrated journalists, broadcasters, media organizations, and digital storytellers whose work has advanced truth, accountability, patriotism, and public service. More than an awards program, the event served as a reaffirmation of the indispensable role that a free and responsible press plays in safeguarding democracy and strengthening the nation.

The evening opened with a stirring Parade of Colors led by the Philippine Coast Guard, followed by the Doxology, the Philippine National Anthem, and the Rotary Club of Manila Hymn. Rotary Club of Manila President Atty. Raoul C. Creencia formally called the meeting to order and welcomed members and guests to a celebration that linked the ideals of Philippine independence with the enduring mission of journalism.
The President’s Message: Freedom Requires Truth

In his welcome remarks and Independence Day toast, President Creencia reminded the gathering that freedom is sustained not only by those who fought for it on the battlefield, but also by those who continue to defend it through the pursuit of truth.

By hosting the Pro Patria Journalism Awards as part of its Independence Day celebration, the Rotary Club of Manila reaffirmed its belief that journalism remains one of the strongest pillars of a democratic society. The evening paid tribute to media practitioners who continue to serve the public interest with courage, integrity, and profession alism amid increasing challenges to truth and public discourse.
The Chairman’s Message: Journalism as Patriotism
The evening’s most reflective address came from Past Director Amado “Amading” Valdez, Chairman of the Pro Patria Journalism Awards.

Valdez recounted how the Rotary Club of Manila decided several years ago to rename the awards “Pro Patria”—Latin for “For Country”— during the presidency of Hermie Esguerra. The decision emerged from a desire to create an Independence Day tradition that would celebrate not only freedom but also those who help preserve it through journalism.

Drawing from the example of the Daily Tribune, which prominently displays its previous Pro Patria award on its masthead, Valdez underscored what the recognition represents: journalism practiced “without fear and without favor.”

He described journalism as a form of storytelling that transcends mere narration. At its highest level, journalism creates history. It gives meaning to events, shapes public memory, and provides future generations with an understanding of their time.
“Journalism,” he observed, “is storytelling with a special purpose.”
Yet for Valdez, technical skill alone is insufficient. The defining quality of great journalists is courage—the willingness to take risks in pursuit of truth, integrity, and hope.

He noted that this common thread united all the evening’s honorees. Whether working in traditional media or digital platforms, they demonstrated a commitment to country that went beyond professional achievement. Their work reflected a willingness to confront difficult truths and to place public service above personal comfort.

In one of the evening’s most moving moments, Valdez shared how, after the passing of his wife, he found renewed optimism and love for the Philippines through travel vlogs that rediscovered the beauty of Northern Luzon. That personal experience ultimately inspired the recognition of the evening’s Vlogger of the Year and underscored the broader message of the awards: journalism and storytelling can deepen our appreciation of country and rekindle hope in difficult times.
The 2026 Pro Patria Journalism Awardees
The Rotary Club of Manila recognized eight outstanding recipients whose work exemplifies the highest standards of journalism and public communication.
Eleazar D. Caldona (Elimotour) - Vlogger of the Year

Through authentic motorcycle journeys into remote communities and hidden destinations across Northern Luzon and the Cordilleras, Elimotour has introduced Filipinos to the country’s natural beauty, cultural richness, and resilient communities.

The award citation praised his raw and honest storytelling, which enables viewers to experience the challenges, triumphs, and wonder of exploration alongside him. His work encourages viewers to rediscover the Philippines and strengthens appreciation for the nation’s heritage.
Bombo Radyo - Radio Station of the Year
For decades, Bombo Radyo has remained one of the country’s most trusted sources of news and public service information.

The citation highlighted its extensive provincial reach, disaster coverage, and community-centered programming that has consistently informed and protected Filipinos during emergencies and crises. Its reputation for public service and meaningful broadcasting has made it a pillar of responsible journalism.
Christian V. Esguerra - Most Outstanding Online Journalist of the Year
Christian Esguerra was honored for elevating public discourse through responsible and impactful digital journalism.

His work promotes truth, accountability, democratic engagement, and critical thinking. Through digital platforms, interviews, and analysis, he has become one of the country's most influential voices in contemporary journalism.
Angelo Palmones - Radio Broadcaster of the Year
A respected veteran broadcaster, Angelo Palmones was recognized for sustaining excellence in radio journalism while preserving the relevance and dignity of the medium.
His work embodies integrity, ethical journalism, and faithful service to country—values central to the spirit of the Pro Patria Awards.
Business Mirror - Newspaper of the Year
BusinessMirror received recognition for its unwavering commitment to development oriented journalism.

Its extensive coverage of business, infrastructure, agriculture, energy, public policy, and economic development has made it an indispensable source of information for both public and private sector leaders. The newspaper was cited for contributing meaningfully to economic understanding and nation-building.
Jarius Ymzon Bondoc - Opinion Writer of the Year
Through his long-running “Gotcha” column and decades of investigative commentary, Jarius Bondoc has consistently promoted accountability, exposed corruption, and stimulated informed public discourse.
The citation recognized his analytical depth, moral courage, and dedication to public service.
GMA Network - Television Station of the Year
GMA Network was honored for delivering some of the country's most comprehensive and credible news and documentary programming.

The citation specifically highlighted its investigative reporting and documentary work, including the internationally acclaimed POGOLAND documentary and its groundbreaking coverage of the flood-control controversy that brought governance issues into national focus.
Alfonso Tomas "Atom" Pagaduan Araullo - Television Journalist of the Year

One of the country's most respected journalists and documentarians, Atom Araullo was recognized for his investigative work through The Atom Araullo Specials: POGOLAND. The documentary received major international recognition while also contributing to meaningful policy discussions and public awareness regarding governance and law enforcement issues.
Voices of Integrity: The Acceptance Speeches
The awardees’ acceptance speeches revealed a common theme: journalism remains both a privilege and a responsibility.
Elimotour: Sharing the Beauty of the Philippines
Receiving the Vlogger of the Year Award, Eleazar Caldona expressed surprise and gratitude for the recognition.

He explained that he began creating content simply to share adventures in remote and little-known destinations. For him, the award was not merely a recognition of his channel but also a tribute to the beauty, culture, and history of Northern Luzon and the Cordilleras.
He pledged to continue telling the stories of the country with pride and love for the nation.
Angelo Palmones: A Beacon of Hope
Angelo Palmones kept his remarks characteristically brief and humorous, joking about the reputation of journalists for delivering long speeches.
BusinessMirror: Pro-Development Journalism

Accepting the Newspaper of the Year Award, BusinessMirror reaffirmed its editorial philosophy of being “pro-development, pro business, and pro-government” while remaining committed to fact based reporting.

Its representative emphasized that despite the many challenges confronting the Philippines, immense opportunities remain. The newspaper's mission, he said, is to help citizens recognize those opportunities while remaining grounded in verified facts and responsible journalism.
Jarius Bondoc: Patriotism as Inheritance
Jarius Bondoc delivered perhaps the evening’s most eloquent and patriotic acceptance speech.

He dedicated the award to his wife, daughter, and longtime assistant before reflecting on the importance of passing patriotism to future generations. Drawing from Andres Bonifacio’s poem Pag-ibig sa Tinubuang Lupa, he reminded the audience that love of country remains among the highest virtues citizens can leave behind.
His speech underscored the connection between journalism and citizenship.
GMA Network: Journalism as a Democratic Institution

Accepting on behalf of GMA Network, Vice President Michelle Seva emphasized that the recognition belonged not only to the network but also to the thousands of journalists and media professionals who serve audiences every day.

She observed that recent events have demonstrated how interconnected societies have become and why trustworthy information remains essential. She stressed that democracy is strongest when citizens have access to facts they can trust and affirmed GMA's commitment to fair, responsible, and independent journalism.
Atom Araullo: Following the Evidence
Atom Araullo reflected on the increasingly difficult environment confronting journalists.

At a time when facts are challenged and misinformation proliferates, he emphasized that the journalist’s duty remains unchanged: to ask questions, follow evidence wherever it leads, and ensure that ordinary voices are heard.

He accepted the award on behalf of the reporters, researchers, producers, editors, camera operators, and news workers who contribute to investigative journalism, recognizing journalism as a collective endeavor.
Christian Esguerra: Credibility in the Digital Age
Christian Esguerra delivered one of the evening’s most thought provoking speeches.
He noted that in today’s digital environment, almost everyone can become a content creator. Yet being believable is not the same as being credible.

Credibility, he argued, is earned through years of disciplined work, adherence to ethical standards, and commitment to truth. Awards such as the Pro Patria recognition, he said, create an obligation to continually prove oneself worthy of public trust.
His remarks served as a powerful reminder that integrity remains journalism’s most valuable asset.
Journalism and the Republic

The 2026 Pro Patria Journalism Awards concluded with a special musical performance by actress and singer Pinky Marquez before President Raoul Creencia delivered the response and formally adjourned the meeting.
More importantly, however, the evening ended with a renewed appreciation for journalism’s role in nation-building.

In honoring broadcasters, reporters, commentators, media organizations, and digital storytellers, the Rotary Club of Manila reaffirmed a principle that remains as relevant today as it was when the nation first won its independence: a free people require truthful information, courageous journalism, and citizens willing to place country above self.
That is the enduring spirit of Pro Patria — For Country.

PDG Alex Cureg’s Valedictory Address  FELLOW Trustees, Manila Rotarians, members of the Foundation, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen: Right off the bat, I would like to thank my esteemed Board of Trustees,for a year well-spent together.Not only was the year well spent -- together, my board and I were able to institute a work culture with a pervasive ethos characterized by responsibility, accountability, and transparency. It is my sincere hope that this ethos will continue to flourish under the capable leadership of incoming Chairman Raoul Creencia, incoming President Mike Roxas and the incoming Board of Trustees. When we began our term, we inherited an organization whose administrative foundations had been shaken by years of neglect. Yet rather than dwell on the difficulties, we chose to confront these challenges. Today, I can say with confidence that the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation stands stronger, more disciplined, more transparent, and better prepared for the future than when we assumed office. Allow me to briefly share some of the milestones we achieved together. Our former Executive Director, Ms. Amy Babiano was requested to step down from office because of her incapability or lack of capability to manage the foundation diligently and efficiently. In this regard, I wish to acknowledge the invaluable assistance of our Board Legal Adviser, Caloy Serapio for sharing his expertise in this delicate process. Personnel concerns were addressed with fairness, professionalism, and due process. Long-standing operational issues were reviewed and resolved, enabling the foundation to function more efficiently and effectively. Given that Ms. Babiano lacked the skills to deliver what the foundation needed, outsourced consultants were hired prior to our term, just like Carie Basila. Some consultants, unfortunately, were less than truthful in their submissions to the government on behalf of the foundation. Because former consultants misrepresented the foundation as a “standard social welfare agency”, this structural misclassification led to inefficiencies, financial ambiguities, and procedural confusion. Our board, guided by our pervasive ethos of good governance, accountability and self-reliance, was able to avoid costly contracts for outsourced consultants and less than competent employees. I recommend that the foundation, in the future, avoid hiring external consultants which are not only costly but are also not entirely reliable. The foundation successfully renewed its authority to issue tax-deductible donation certificates to our benefactors. This accomplishment was achieved without reliance on costly external consultants and was made possible through the efforts of my spouse, Atty. Anna Cureg, our treasurer Mike Roxas and Star Rotarian Chris Tamesis. We were successful in having the Bureau of Internal Revenue recognize that indeed, our foundation is deserving of this privilege despite that we do not belong under the purview of the Department of Social Welfare and Development as we are a mere resource agency and not a social welfare agency in the strict sense of the term. A major accomplishment of this Board was the clarification of the foundation's institutional identity. We reaffirmed that the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation exists primarily as a resource-generating institution that supports the service projects of the Rotary Club of Manila across Rotary's Seven Areas of Focus. This distinction was important. By defining our role clearly, we were able to align our governance structure, compliance requirements, and operational priorities with our true mission. In doing so, we strengthened our credibility with regulators, donors, and stakeholders alike. We instituted office protocols that restored order and accountability within the secretariat, especially introducing metrics for performance. For example, our staff, which right now is composed of just Jonathan, is required to submit overtime requests. Faced with disarrayed records and compliance gaps, we spearheaded the digitalization of records via Google Drive, envisioning a future where every transaction, contract and report, could be retrieved with ease and efficiency. For the first time in years, institutional memory is preserved, not in dusty filing cabinets, but through digital archiving. For purposes of good governance and corporate housekeeping, I requested Atty. Anna to create a New Manual of Operations, which manual was duly adopted and approved by the board and applied meaningfully through-out our term. This new manual was transformative. It is pragmatic, easy to-follow and designed not just for regulation, but for lasting institutional discipline. Good governance should not just be a buzzword but a daily and consistent practice. This new manual,in part, highlighted the importance of accountability and transparency in the funding of service projects. Included were the project evaluation and monitoring systems. Clear criteria and scoring mechanisms were implemented to ensure that funded projects aligned with the foundation's objectives, complied with regulatory requirements, and delivered measurable social impact. Likewise, enhanced fund utilization reporting requirements ensured that every peso entrusted to us was properly accounted for. For his diligent oversight of this process, I extend my appreciation to Project Evaluation Committee Chairman Bertel Ingmar Bertelsen. Financial discipline remained a central priority throughout the year. To ensure that the foundation’s fiscal position continues to be stable and strategic, the board, through Treasurer Mike Roxas engaged Racuya Business Solutions to professionalize accounting operations, implement prudent internal controls, and adopt best practices in financial reporting. Our approach to finance was both conservative and visionary. To safeguard restricted funds while generating income, the foundation made a landmark investment of Php5,000,000.00 in a low-risk time deposit. Every peso we hold carries the trust of our donors and members. It is our responsibility to multiply it– not through risk, but through prudence. As of date, this investment already earned Php129,195.55 since its original placement. It was not my intention to let problems fester. There were, allegedly, unpaid contributions and penalties to the Social Security System, which issue was pending since 2019. Again sharing his exceptional expertise, financial genius, Treasurer Mike Roxas was able to resolve this issue with finality with the SSS giving the foundation a clean slate. Given the problems that we faced, we had to overhaul the foundation’s management model, replacing consultant-driven operations with board-centered governance, a structure that placed accountability squarely where it belonged: in the hands of the elected trustees and not on the whims of the secretariat or outsourced directors. Our board was not just a ceremonial body, but a working one – hands-on,pro-active, and guided by the spirit of fiduciary stewardship. Our board functioned as a cohesive, decision-making unit and we met regularly. We held seven productive meetings, three over the mere four that were required by our by-laws. Proudly, I can say we encountered no quorum problems. At this point, I again have to express my gratitude to our board for their cooperation, support and dedication. Inspired by the brainchild of Past Chairman Lito Sibayan, an initiative called the Legacy Endowment Fund was launched during last year’s induction ceremony. This fund, which was supported by our generous members is meant to ensure the continued viability of our foundation and further its lofty mission in helping others. Let us please give a resounding applause to all those who contributed generously. We are not nearly done. Vice President Elect Karlo Castro chairs the 4 RCMFI Golf Tournament committee and his team intend to raise a hefty Php 6 million to make the foundation’s financial standing even more robust. Meanwhile, through the efforts of Membership Chairman Chito Zaldarriaga, our membership continued to grow, reaching 164 members after welcoming 16 new Foundation members during the year. Finally, I proudly present to you the successful projects accomplished through the funding support given by the foundation. Please direct your attention to the screen. The foundation’s humanitarian reach expanded across multiple provinces and causes, directly impacting hundreds of families, communities, and even animal companions. Each initiative reflects the foundation’s guiding principle: that service must be inclusive, responsive, and rooted in empathy. Conclusion I could go on and on with unbridled passion on how serving this institution became one of the meaningful experiences in my years as a Rotarian, but I won’t. Instead, I pass the torch to incoming Chairman Raoul Creencia, incoming President Mike Roxas and the next Board of Trustees, with optimism and confidence. I leave you with the hope that its future leaders continue to nurture this foundation with what we Filipinos beautifully call malasakit— that deep sense of care, ownership, and responsibility that transforms duty into service. To my fellow Trustees, thank you for an unforgettable year. Together, we strengthened the foundation's legal standing, we improved its operational systems, we reinforced its financial position, we established governance structures that will benefit future generations of Manila Rotarians and most importantly, we demonstrated that stewardship matters. Leadership is temporary. Institutions endure. The true responsibility of every trustee is not merely to manage the foundation during his term, but to leave it stronger than he found it. I believe we have done exactly that. To our members and donors, thank you for your trust. And to the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation, may your finest years still lie ahead. God bless the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation, Inc. God bless Rotary Club of Manila. Mabuhay! 36th Weekly Membership Meeting Program  Thursday, June 25, 2026, 12:00 PM

PRES. RAOUL C. CREENCIA 2026 CLUB AWARDS | Celebrating Excellence, Service, and Commitment: RCM Honors Outstanding Members for Rotary Year 2025–2026 PE Reginald T. Yu AS Rotary Year 2025–2026 comes to a close, the Rotary Club of Manila once again reaffirmed its tradition of recognizing excellence, dedication, and service through its annual Club Awards Program. More than a ceremony of recognition, the awards serve as a celebration of the values that have sustained Asia’s first Rotary club for over a century — commitment, fellowship, leadership, loyalty, and Service Above Self. The Club Awards recognize members whose actions throughout the year have strengthened the organization and advanced its mission of making a meaningful difference in the lives of others. From exemplary participation in club activities to decades of unwavering commitment, the honorees represent the very best of what it means to be a Manila Rotarian. One of the highlights of the awards program was the presentation of the Best Attendance Awards, honoring members who consistently demonstrated their dedication by actively participating in weekly membership meetings, board meetings, service projects, fellowship activities, and other club functions throughout the Rotary year. While attendance may appear to be a simple measure, it reflects a deeper commitment to the life of the club. Strong participation fosters fellowship, strengthens camaraderie, and ensures that members remain engaged in the planning and execution of meaningful service initiatives. The Club also paid tribute to members whose long-standing dedication has helped preserve the traditions and institutional memory of the organization through the Legacy and Loyalty Awards. These recognitions were bestowed upon Rotarians who have devoted significant portions of their lives to the Rotary Club of Manila, with milestones ranging from fifteen to forty-five years of membership. Such longevity is a remarkable achievement in itself. Beyond the years, however, these awards recognize the countless hours devoted to service projects, mentorship, leadership, fundraising, community development, and club administration. These Rotarians have witnessed the club's evolution through changing times while remaining steadfast in their commitment to Rotary’s ideals. Their dedication has helped shape generations of leaders and ensured that the Rotary Club of Manila remains a vibrant and relevant institution more than a century after its founding. Equally inspiring was the presentation of the Rising Manila Rotarian Awards, which recognize newer members who have quickly distinguished themselves through active participation, leadership potential, initiative, and a strong commitment to Rotary values. These awardees represent the next generation of leaders who will carry forward the proud traditions of the club while bringing fresh ideas, new energy, and innovative approaches to service. 2026 Club Awards The recognition of emerging leaders reflects the Club’s commitment to continuity and succession. By encouraging newer members to become actively involved early in their Rotary journey, the Rotary Club of Manila ensures that its legacy of service will continue to flourish for generations to come. Taken together, the various awards highlight the diverse ways in which members contribute to the success of the organization. Some lead through decades of faithful service. Others contribute through consistent participation and engagement. Still others distinguish themselves through enthusiasm, initiative, and emerging leadership. Each contribution, regardless of form, plays a vital role in strengthening the Club and expanding its impact on the communities it serves. The annual Club Awards also serve as a reminder that Rotary is ultimately a people-centered organization. Projects may define the Club’s public impact, but it is the dedication, generosity, and commitment of its members that make those projects possible. Behind every successful initiative, every community service project, every scholarship program, and every humanitarian effort are Rotarians who willingly give their time, talents, and resources in pursuit of a greater purpose. As the Rotary Club of Manila prepares to embark on a new Rotary year, the accomplishments celebrated through the 2025–2026 Club Awards provide both inspiration and motivation. The awardees embody the values that have guided the Club for more than a century and serve as examples for future generations of Manila Rotarians. Their stories remind us that Rotary’s enduring strength lies not only in its history but in the continued commitment of its members to live out the ideal of Service Above Self. Through their dedication, leadership, and unwavering spirit of fellowship, they help ensure that the Rotary Club of Manila remains a force for good, creating lasting impact in the Philippines and beyond. Honoring the Faces of Service This year's Club Awardees represent the very best of the Rotary Club of Manila — individuals whose dedication, leadership, loyalty, and commitment to Service Above Self have helped strengthen the Club and advance its mission throughout Rotary Year 2025–2026. Among them are members whose exemplary attendance reflects an unwavering commitment to fellowship and engagement; veteran Rotarians whose decades of faithful service have preserved and enriched the Club's proud legacy; and emerging leaders whose enthusiasm, initiative, and active participation embody the future of Asia's first Rotary club. Collectively, these awardees remind us that Rotary's greatest asset is not its history, projects, or achievements, but the men and women who willingly devote their time, talents, and resources to serving others. Through their example, they inspire fellow Rotarians to continue building a stronger Club and a more compassionate society. The Rotary Club of Manila proudly recognizes these outstanding members whose contributions have made a lasting impact on the Club and the communities it serves. Rotary Club of Manila Concludes Rotary Year with Meaningful 35th Weekly Membership Meeting PE Reginald T. Yu THE Rotary Club of Manila (RCM) gathered at the Manila Polo Club for its 35th Weekly Membership Meeting of Rotary Year 2025–2026, an afternoon marked by reflection, accountability, and inspiration. The meeting featured two highly anticipated presentations: the year-end report of the RCManila Foundation, Inc. (RCMFI) delivered by Chairman PDG Alexander P. Cureg, and the Classification Talk of Star Rotarian Manuel E. “AJ” Pangilinan, Chief Executive Officer of Finasiatech Corporation. Presided over by Rotary Club of Manila President Raoul C. Creencia, the meeting brought together members, guests, and trustees to celebrate a year of accomplishments while looking toward new opportunities for service and leadership. President Raoul Highlights Club Initiatives In his message to the membership, President Raoul Creencia shared updates on key club initiatives and ongoing projects, including preparations for the forthcoming RCM Golf Cup and various service activities supported by the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation. The gathering also included presentations related to the club’s fundraising efforts, underscoring the importance of sustainable resource generation in advancing Rotary’s mission of service above self. Trustee and Treasurer Michael Roxas presented the Foundation’s financial report, providing members with an overview of the organization’s fiscal position before the presentation of the Foundation’s comprehensive year-end accomplishments. Special Report: PDG Alex Cureg Presents Transformative Year-End Report of the RCManila Foundation The centerpiece of the meeting was the valedictory presentation of PDG Alexander P. Cureg, who reflected on a year defined by organizational reform, strengthened governance, financial stewardship, and impactful humanitarian service. Building a Culture of Accountability and Transparency PDG Cureg opened his report by expressing gratitude to the Board of Trustees for embracing a culture rooted in responsibility, accountabi lity, and transparency. He noted that when the Board assumed leadership, the Foundation faced significant administrative and operational challenges. Rather than allowing these issues to persist, the Board undertook a comprehensive effort to rebuild and strengthen the institution. Through a series of reforms, the Foundation clarified its institutional identity as a resource-generating organization whose primary mission is to support the service projects of the Rotary Club of Manila. This distinction enabled the Foundation to align its governance structure, compliance requirements, and operational priorities more effectively. The Board also streamlined personnel and administrative processes, improved office protocols, and instituted performance measures that restored discipline and accountability within the organization. Modernizing Foundation Operations One of the year’s notable accomplishments was the digitalization of Foundation records. By transitioning documents and institutional files into a centralized digital archive, the Foundation preserved its institutional memory and improved accessibility, efficiency, and continuity for future leaders. Complementing this initiative was the adoption of a new Manual of Operations, which established clear governance standards and practical procedures for the organization. Designed to be both comprehensive and user-friendly, the manual provides a framework for sustaining good governance practices well into the future. Strengthening Project Evaluation and Governance Recognizing the importance of responsible stewardship, the Foundation implemented a more rigorous project evaluation and monitoring framework. Under this system, all funding requests were subjected to objective scoring criteria, ensuring alignment with Foundation priorities, regulatory compliance, and measurable social impact. Enhanced reporting requirements were likewise introduced to guarantee transparency and accountability in the utilization of Foundation resources. These reforms represented a significant step toward ensuring that every peso entrusted to the Foundation generates meaningful and measurable benefits for communities in need. Financial Stewardship and Long-Term Sustainability Financial discipline remained a cornerstone of the Foundation’s strategy throughout the year. Among its major achievements was the successful renewal of the Foundation’s authority to issue tax deductible donation certificates, a development that strengthens its ability to attract philanthropic support. The Foundation also resolved long-standing compliance concerns and improved its accounting and financial reporting systems through enhanced internal controls and professionalized financial management practices. To preserve and grow donor resources responsibly, the Foundation invested ₱5 million in a low-risk time deposit, generating additional income while safeguarding principal funds. This prudent approach reflects the Board’s commitment to balancing stability with sustainability. body.text: FELLOW Trustees, Manila Rotarians, members of the Foundation, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen:

Right off the bat, I would like to thank my esteemed Board of Trustees,for a year well-spent together.Not only was the year well spent -- together, my board and I were able to institute a work culture with a pervasive ethos characterized by responsibility, accountability, and transparency. It is my sincere hope that this ethos will continue to flourish under the capable leadership of incoming Chairman Raoul Creencia, incoming President Mike Roxas and the incoming Board of Trustees.

When we began our term, we inherited an organization whose administrative foundations had been shaken by years of neglect. Yet rather than dwell on the difficulties, we chose to confront these challenges.
Today, I can say with confidence that the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation stands stronger, more disciplined, more transparent, and better prepared for the future than when we assumed office.
Allow me to briefly share some of the milestones we achieved together.

Our former Executive Director, Ms. Amy Babiano was requested to step down from office because of her incapability or lack of capability to manage the foundation diligently and efficiently. In this regard, I wish to acknowledge the invaluable assistance of our Board Legal Adviser, Caloy Serapio for sharing his expertise in this delicate process. Personnel concerns were addressed with fairness, professionalism, and due process. Long-standing operational issues were reviewed and resolved, enabling the foundation to function more efficiently and effectively.

Given that Ms. Babiano lacked the skills to deliver what the foundation needed, outsourced consultants were hired prior to our term, just like Carie Basila. Some consultants, unfortunately, were less than truthful in their submissions to the government on behalf of the foundation. Because former consultants misrepresented the foundation as a “standard social welfare agency”, this structural misclassification led to inefficiencies, financial ambiguities, and procedural confusion.

Our board, guided by our pervasive ethos of good governance, accountability and self-reliance, was able to avoid costly contracts for outsourced consultants and less than competent employees. I recommend that the foundation, in the future, avoid hiring external consultants which are not only costly but are also not entirely reliable.

The foundation successfully renewed its authority to issue tax-deductible donation certificates to our benefactors. This accomplishment was achieved without reliance on costly external consultants and was made possible through the efforts of my spouse, Atty. Anna Cureg, our treasurer Mike Roxas and Star Rotarian Chris Tamesis. We were successful in having the Bureau of Internal Revenue recognize that indeed, our foundation is deserving of this privilege despite that we do not belong under the purview of the Department of Social Welfare and Development as we are a mere resource agency and not a social welfare agency in the strict sense of the term.

A major accomplishment of this Board was the clarification of the foundation's institutional identity. We reaffirmed that the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation exists primarily as a resource-generating institution that supports the service projects of the Rotary Club of Manila across Rotary's Seven Areas of Focus. This distinction was important. By defining our role clearly, we were able to align our governance structure, compliance requirements, and operational priorities with our true mission. In doing so, we strengthened our credibility with regulators, donors, and stakeholders alike.

We instituted office protocols that restored order and accountability within the secretariat, especially introducing metrics for performance. For example, our staff, which right now is composed of just Jonathan, is required to submit overtime requests.

Faced with disarrayed records and compliance gaps, we spearheaded the digitalization of records via Google Drive, envisioning a future where every transaction, contract and report, could be retrieved with ease and efficiency. For the first time in years, institutional memory is preserved, not in dusty filing cabinets, but through digital archiving.

For purposes of good governance and corporate housekeeping, I requested Atty. Anna to create a New Manual of Operations, which manual was duly adopted and approved by the board and applied meaningfully through-out our term. This new manual was transformative. It is pragmatic, easy to-follow and designed not just for regulation, but for lasting institutional discipline. Good governance should not just be a buzzword but a daily and consistent practice.

This new manual,in part, highlighted the importance of accountability and transparency in the funding of service projects. Included were the project evaluation and monitoring systems. Clear criteria and scoring mechanisms were implemented to ensure that funded projects aligned with the foundation's objectives, complied with regulatory requirements, and delivered measurable social impact. Likewise, enhanced fund utilization reporting requirements ensured that every peso entrusted to us was properly accounted for. For his diligent oversight of this process, I extend my appreciation to Project Evaluation Committee Chairman Bertel Ingmar Bertelsen.

Financial discipline remained a central priority throughout the year. To ensure that the foundation’s fiscal position continues to be stable and strategic, the board, through Treasurer Mike Roxas engaged Racuya Business Solutions to professionalize accounting operations, implement prudent internal controls, and adopt best practices in financial reporting.

Our approach to finance was both conservative and visionary. To safeguard restricted funds while generating income, the foundation made a landmark investment of Php5,000,000.00 in a low-risk time deposit. Every peso we hold carries the trust of our donors and members. It is our responsibility to multiply it– not through risk, but through prudence. As of date, this investment already earned Php129,195.55 since its original placement.

It was not my intention to let problems fester. There were, allegedly, unpaid contributions and penalties to the Social Security System, which issue was pending since 2019. Again sharing his exceptional expertise, financial genius, Treasurer Mike Roxas was able to resolve this issue with finality with the SSS giving the foundation a clean slate.

Given the problems that we faced, we had to overhaul the foundation’s management model, replacing consultant-driven operations with board-centered governance, a structure that placed accountability squarely where it belonged: in the hands of the elected trustees and not on the whims of the secretariat or outsourced directors. Our board was not just a ceremonial body, but a working one – hands-on,pro-active, and guided by the spirit of fiduciary stewardship.

Our board functioned as a cohesive, decision-making unit and we met regularly. We held seven productive meetings, three over the mere four that were required by our by-laws. Proudly, I can say we encountered no quorum problems. At this point, I again have to express my gratitude to our board for their cooperation, support and dedication.

Inspired by the brainchild of Past Chairman Lito Sibayan, an initiative called the Legacy Endowment Fund was launched during last year’s induction ceremony. This fund, which was supported by our generous members is meant to ensure the continued viability of our foundation and further its lofty mission in helping others. Let us please give a resounding applause to all those who contributed generously.

We are not nearly done. Vice President Elect Karlo Castro chairs the 4 RCMFI Golf Tournament committee and his team intend to raise a hefty Php 6 million to make the foundation’s financial standing even more robust.
Meanwhile, through the efforts of Membership Chairman Chito Zaldarriaga, our membership continued to grow, reaching 164 members after welcoming 16 new Foundation members during the year.

Finally, I proudly present to you the successful projects accomplished through the funding support given by the foundation. Please direct your attention to the screen. The foundation’s humanitarian reach expanded across multiple provinces and causes, directly impacting hundreds of families, communities, and even animal companions. Each initiative reflects the foundation’s guiding principle: that service must be inclusive, responsive, and rooted in empathy.
Conclusion

I could go on and on with unbridled passion on how serving this institution became one of the meaningful experiences in my years as a Rotarian, but I won’t. Instead, I pass the torch to incoming Chairman Raoul Creencia, incoming President Mike Roxas and the next Board of Trustees, with optimism and confidence. I leave you with the hope that its future leaders continue to nurture this foundation with what we Filipinos beautifully call malasakit— that deep sense of care, ownership, and responsibility that transforms duty into service.

To my fellow Trustees, thank you for an unforgettable year. Together, we strengthened the foundation's legal standing, we improved its operational systems, we reinforced its financial position, we established governance structures that will benefit future generations of Manila Rotarians and most importantly, we demonstrated that stewardship matters. Leadership is temporary. Institutions endure. The true responsibility of every trustee is not merely to manage the foundation during his term, but to leave it stronger than he found it. I believe we have done exactly that.
To our members and donors, thank you for your trust.
And to the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation, may your finest years still lie ahead. God bless the Rotary Club of Manila Foundation, Inc. God bless Rotary Club of Manila.
Mabuhay!
